rules.section: Foreword & Clauses 3–4: Basic Welding Symbols, Standard Element Locations, and Joint Types
rules.title: Prohibition of Blanket 'Weld Throughout' / 'Completely Welded' Notes
rules.audit_check: Drawings SHOULD NOT use vague blanket notes such as 'to be welded throughout' or 'to be completely welded', which improperly transfer design responsibility from the designer to production personnel.
rules.pass_condition: All welded joints are defined by explicit AWS A2.4 welding symbols (or referenced weld procedures/tables) specifying weld type, location, size, and extent.
rules.fail_condition: Drawing relies on vague general statements like 'weld throughout' or 'completely weld assembly' without explicit welding symbols or sizing.
rules.remediation: Replace blanket welding notes with complete AWS A2.4 welding symbols specifying weld type, size, location, and extent for every joint.

rules.section: Foreword & Clauses 3–4: Basic Welding Symbols, Standard Element Locations, and Joint Types
rules.title: Distinction Between Weld Symbol and Welding Symbol
rules.audit_check: A weld symbol indicates only the type of weld and, when used, is a component of the complete welding symbol (reference line, arrow, and optional elements).
rules.pass_condition: Weld type glyphs are always attached to a complete welding symbol with a horizontal reference line and arrow pointing to the joint.
rules.fail_condition: Standalone weld type glyphs float on the drawing without a reference line or arrow connecting them to a joint.
rules.remediation: Assemble every weld symbol onto a complete welding symbol containing a horizontal reference line and an arrow pointing unambiguously to the joint.

rules.section: Foreword & Clauses 3–4: Basic Welding Symbols, Standard Element Locations, and Joint Types
rules.title: Joint as Basis of Reference — Arrow Side vs. Other Side
rules.audit_check: The joint is the basis of reference: the arrow side is the side of the joint to which the arrow points, and the other side is the side of the joint opposite the arrow side.
rules.pass_condition: Arrow termination clearly identifies one side of the joint so arrow-side and other-side weld callouts map unambiguously to physical joint faces.
rules.fail_condition: Arrow points ambiguously to an edge or hidden geometry where arrow side vs. other side cannot be conclusively determined.
rules.remediation: Re-route the arrow to contact the clearly visible outer surface or joint line in a view where arrow side and other side are unambiguous.

rules.section: Foreword & Clauses 3–4: Basic Welding Symbols, Standard Element Locations, and Joint Types
rules.title: Standard Weld Symbol Glyphs Must Contact Reference Line
rules.audit_check: Weld symbols SHALL conform to AWS A2.4 Figure 1 (square, scarf, V, bevel, U, J, flare-V, flare-bevel, fillet, plug, slot, stud, spot/projection, seam, back/backing, surfacing, edge) and SHALL be drawn in direct contact with the reference line.
rules.pass_condition: Every weld symbol uses a standard Figure 1 glyph drawn directly touching the horizontal reference line (or centered on it where no side significance applies).
rules.fail_condition: Non-standard/invented weld glyphs are used, or a weld symbol floats detached from the reference line with a visible gap.
rules.remediation: Use standard AWS A2.4 Figure 1 weld glyphs and snap each weld symbol into direct contact with the horizontal reference line.

rules.section: Foreword & Clauses 3–4: Basic Welding Symbols, Standard Element Locations, and Joint Types
rules.title: Standard Supplementary Welding Symbols (Figure 2)
rules.audit_check: Supplementary symbols used with welding symbols (weld-all-around circle, field weld flag, melt-through, square consumable insert, rectangular backing, rectangular spacer, and flush/flat, convex, or concave contour symbols) SHALL conform to Figure 2.
rules.pass_condition: All supplementary glyphs match AWS A2.4 Figure 2 shapes and conventions.
rules.fail_condition: Ad-hoc or non-standard supplementary shapes (e.g., filled triangles for contour, non-standard backing shapes, or open flags) are used.
rules.remediation: Replace non-standard supplementary symbols with the exact graphical forms defined in AWS A2.4 Figure 2.

rules.section: Foreword & Clauses 3–4: Basic Welding Symbols, Standard Element Locations, and Joint Types
rules.title: Required Elements (Reference Line & Arrow) and Standard Locations (Figure 3)
rules.audit_check: Every welding symbol SHALL include at minimum a reference line and an arrow; all optional elements (size/depth S(E), root opening/fill R, groove/countersink angle A, contour, finishing designator F, length-pitch L-P, weld count (N), field/all-around, tail T) SHALL be placed strictly in their AWS A2.4 Figure 3 standard locations.
rules.pass_condition: Reference line and arrow are present, and every included dimensional or supplementary element occupies its exact Figure 3 slot (elements in the central area stay in the same left-to-right order even when arrow and tail are reversed).
rules.fail_condition: Size, length, pitch, angle, root opening, count, or finishing letter is placed in the wrong position (e.g., length placed to the left of symbol, size to the right, or order mirrored when arrow points left vs. right).
rules.remediation: Relocate all welding symbol elements to their mandatory AWS A2.4 Figure 3 positions regardless of whether the arrow connects to the left or right end of the reference line.

rules.section: Foreword & Clauses 3–4: Basic Welding Symbols, Standard Element Locations, and Joint Types
rules.title: Weld Symbols Contained Within Reference Line Length — Never at Ends
rules.audit_check: Weld symbols SHALL be contained within the length of the horizontal reference line and SHALL NOT be placed at either end of the reference line (arrow junction or tail junction).
rules.pass_condition: Weld symbols sit cleanly along the interior span of the reference line with clear separation from the arrow junction and tail.
rules.fail_condition: A weld symbol touches or sits directly on the arrow-to-reference-line junction or tail end of the reference line.
rules.remediation: Extend the horizontal reference line and reposition the weld symbol cleanly inside its length, away from both ends.

rules.section: Foreword & Clauses 3–4: Basic Welding Symbols, Standard Element Locations, and Joint Types
rules.title: Arrow Must Conclusively Identify Joint, Location, or Area
rules.audit_check: The arrow of the welding symbol SHALL point to a line, location, or area that conclusively identifies the joint, location, or area to be welded.
rules.pass_condition: Arrowhead terminates directly on a joint line, weld centerline, or clearly bounded surface/area with zero ambiguity.
rules.fail_condition: Arrowhead stops in empty space, points vaguely near multiple adjacent joints, or points to a view border instead of the actual joint.
rules.remediation: Snap the welding symbol arrowhead directly onto the exact joint line, intersection, or defined weld area.

rules.section: Foreword & Clauses 3–4: Basic Welding Symbols, Standard Element Locations, and Joint Types
rules.title: Basic Joint Types and Table A.1 Joint Designators
rules.audit_check: When basic joint types are designated by letter codes on drawings, tails, or weld tables, they SHALL match AWS A2.4 Clause 4 and Table A.1: B (Butt), C (Corner), T (T-joint), L (Lap), E (Edge).
rules.pass_condition: Joint type designators in tails, schedules, or joint IDs strictly use B, C, T, L, or E consistent with physical joint geometry.
rules.fail_condition: Non-standard joint letter codes are used, or a joint designator contradicts the depicted joint geometry (e.g., calling a lap joint 'B').
rules.remediation: Correct joint type letter designators to match AWS A2.4 Table A.1 (B, C, T, L, E) and verify consistency with the drawn joint geometry.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Arrow-Side Information Below Reference Line; Other-Side Above
rules.audit_check: All weld symbols and dimensions applicable to the arrow side of a joint SHALL be placed below the reference line; all information applicable to the other side of a joint SHALL be placed above the reference line.
rules.pass_condition: Arrow-side weld symbols and their dimensions lie exclusively below the reference line, and other-side weld symbols and dimensions lie exclusively above it.
rules.fail_condition: Arrow-side weld information is placed above the reference line (e.g., inverted ISO Method B style on an AWS drawing) or dimensions are split across opposite sides from their weld symbol.
rules.remediation: Place arrow-side weld symbols and dimensions below the solid horizontal reference line and other-side information above it.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Arrow Contact for Fillet, Groove, and Edge Weld Symbols
rules.audit_check: For fillet, groove, and edge weld symbols, the arrow SHALL contact the outer surface of one of the joints, establishing that side as the arrow side and the opposite side as the other side.
rules.pass_condition: Arrowhead contacts the outer surface line of the joint so arrow side and other side are unambiguously defined.
rules.fail_condition: Arrowhead points to the interior of a plate or fails to touch the joint outer surface line.
rules.remediation: Terminate the arrow directly on the outer surface line of the fillet, groove, or edge joint.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Arrow Contact at Weld Centerline for Plug, Slot, Spot, Projection, and Seam Welds
rules.audit_check: For plug, slot, spot, projection, and seam weld symbols, the arrow SHALL contact the outer surface of one joint member at the centerline of the desired weld, designating that member as the arrow-side member.
rules.pass_condition: Arrowhead touches the outer surface of the member directly at the weld centerline (or intersecting centerlines).
rules.fail_condition: Arrow points to a member edge away from the weld centerline, leaving weld placement or arrow-side member ambiguous.
rules.remediation: Point the arrow to the outer surface of the arrow-side member directly on the centerline of the plug, slot, spot, projection, or seam weld.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Symbols with No Side Significance Centered on Reference Line
rules.audit_check: Weld symbols with no arrow-side or other-side significance (such as resistance spot RSW, resistance seam RSEW, or flash welding FW) are centered on the reference line, although supplementary symbols (e.g., flush/convex contour) used with them may still carry arrow-side or other-side significance.
rules.pass_condition: Side-neutral weld symbols are centered across the reference line while any side-specific contour/finishing symbols are placed above or below as required.
rules.fail_condition: A centered weld symbol is combined with an ambiguous contour placement or used for a process that actually requires arrow-side/other-side specification (e.g., PW projection welding or GTAW spot).
rules.remediation: Keep side-neutral process symbols (RSW, RSEW, FW) centered on the reference line, place side-specific contours on the applicable side, and move side-dependent symbols above or below the line.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Arrow-Side Weld Symbol Below Reference Line
rules.audit_check: Welds on the arrow side of the joint SHALL be specified by placing the weld symbol below the reference line.
rules.pass_condition: Every single-sided weld intended on the side touched by the arrow is drawn below the reference line.
rules.fail_condition: A weld depicted or required on the arrow side is drawn above the reference line.
rules.remediation: Move the arrow-side weld symbol below the reference line (or move the arrow to point to the opposite side of the joint).

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Other-Side Weld Symbol Above Reference Line
rules.audit_check: Welds on the other side of the joint SHALL be specified by placing the weld symbol above the reference line.
rules.pass_condition: Every single-sided weld intended on the side opposite the arrow is drawn above the reference line.
rules.fail_condition: A weld intended on the side opposite the arrow is drawn below the reference line.
rules.remediation: Move the other-side weld symbol above the reference line.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Both-Sides Weld Symbols Below and Above Reference Line
rules.audit_check: Welds on both sides of the joint SHALL be specified by placing weld symbols both below and above the reference line.
rules.pass_condition: Double-sided welds show weld symbols on both sides of the reference line rather than relying on notes or weld-all-around misuse.
rules.fail_condition: A double-sided weld omits one symbol and relies on 'BOTH SIDES' text or a weld-all-around circle instead of placing symbols above and below the reference line.
rules.remediation: Place the applicable weld symbol both below and above the reference line to specify welds on both sides of the joint.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Symmetrical Both-Sides Weld Symbols Must Align Along Symmetry Axis
rules.audit_check: When weld symbols on both sides of the reference line each have an axis of symmetry perpendicular to the reference line (e.g., V, U, square, flare-V), their symmetry axes SHALL be directly aligned across the reference line (staggered intermittent welds are the sole exception).
rules.pass_condition: Symmetrical top and bottom weld symbols align vertically on a shared axis unless explicitly depicting staggered intermittent welds.
rules.fail_condition: Continuous or chain-intermittent symmetrical weld symbols are horizontally offset across the reference line, falsely implying staggered intermittent welding.
rules.remediation: Align the vertical axes of symmetry of both-sides symmetrical weld symbols directly across the reference line.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Nonsymmetrical Both-Sides Weld Symbols Must Align Along Left Side
rules.audit_check: If either weld symbol on opposite sides of the reference line lacks an axis of symmetry perpendicular to the reference line (e.g., fillet, bevel, J, flare-bevel, or mixed square + J), the left sides of both symbols SHALL be directly aligned across the reference line (except staggered intermittent welds).
rules.pass_condition: Left vertical edges of nonsymmetrical or mixed both-sides weld symbols align vertically across the reference line.
rules.fail_condition: Nonsymmetrical continuous/chain weld symbols are centered or misaligned horizontally across the reference line.
rules.remediation: Align the left sides (perpendicular legs) of both-sides nonsymmetrical weld symbols vertically across the reference line.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Perpendicular Leg of Fillet, Bevel, J, and Flare-Bevel Symbols Always to the Left
rules.audit_check: Fillet, bevel-groove, J-groove, and flare-bevel-groove weld symbols SHALL ALWAYS be drawn with the perpendicular (vertical) leg to the left, regardless of arrow direction or physical joint orientation.
rules.pass_condition: Every fillet, bevel-groove, J-groove, and flare-bevel-groove symbol has its vertical leg on the left side and inclined/curved leg extending to the right.
rules.fail_condition: A fillet, bevel-groove, J-groove, or flare-bevel-groove symbol is mirrored horizontally with its perpendicular leg drawn on the right.
rules.remediation: Flip the weld symbol horizontally so the perpendicular leg is strictly on the left.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Broken Arrow for Bevel-Groove and J-Groove Member Selection
rules.audit_check: When only one member of a joint is to receive a bevel-groove or J-groove (or both), the arrow SHALL have one distinct break and point toward that prepared member—except when it is already geometrically apparent which member is prepared; the arrow SHALL NOT be broken if there is no preference as to which member is prepared.
rules.pass_condition: A single-break arrow points unambiguously to the member receiving bevel/J preparation when not obvious; straight arrow is used when either member is acceptable or preparation is obvious (e.g., T-joint web).
rules.fail_condition: A butt joint specifies a single/double bevel or J-groove on a specific member without a broken arrow, or uses a broken arrow when no member preference exists, or has multiple confusing breaks.
rules.remediation: Add a single break in the arrow pointing directly to the member requiring bevel/J preparation, or straighten the arrow if either member may be prepared.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Optional Break in Arrow for Fillet Welds
rules.audit_check: For fillet welds, the arrow may be straight or broken as needed to clearly reach and identify the fillet weld joint location.
rules.pass_condition: Arrow cleanly reaches the fillet joint without crossing clutter or creating ambiguity with bevel preparation.
rules.fail_condition: A broken arrow on a fillet weld points ambiguously away from the intended joint corner.
rules.remediation: Route the straight or broken arrow directly to the intended fillet weld joint corner.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Individual Symbol Required for Each Weld Type in Combination Welds
rules.audit_check: For joints requiring more than one weld type (e.g., bevel-groove plus fillet, or J-groove plus backing weld plus fillet), a distinct weld symbol SHALL be drawn to specify each weld type.
rules.pass_condition: Each weld type on the joint is explicitly represented by its own Figure 1 weld symbol stacked/combined properly on the reference line(s) with its own dimensions.
rules.fail_condition: A combined groove-and-fillet joint omits one of the weld symbols and mentions the second weld only informally or leaves it implied in a cross section.
rules.remediation: Add the standard Figure 1 weld symbol and dimensions for every weld type required at the joint.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Multiple Arrow Lines Only for Identical Welds
rules.audit_check: Two or more arrow lines may originate from a single reference line ONLY when identical welds (same type, size, side significance, and requirements) are specified at each pointed location.
rules.pass_condition: All joints pointed to by arrows sharing a single reference line require the exact same weld type, size, contour, and side orientation.
rules.fail_condition: Multiple arrows from one reference line point to joints with different weld types, sizes, or flipped arrow-side/other-side access.
rules.remediation: Split differing joints onto separate welding symbols rather than sharing a single reference line.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Sequence of Operations Read From Reference Line Nearest Arrow Outward
rules.audit_check: When multiple reference lines are used, the first operation is specified on the reference line nearest the arrow, and subsequent operations are read sequentially moving outward away from the arrow.
rules.pass_condition: Sequential operations (e.g., backing weld -> groove weld -> backgouge/fillet -> NDE) are ordered strictly from the reference line closest to the arrow outward.
rules.fail_condition: Operations on multiple reference lines are placed in reverse or physically impossible order (e.g., NDE or final fillet placed closer to the arrow than the underlying groove weld).
rules.remediation: Reorder the multiple reference lines so the first operation is on the line nearest the arrowhead and each subsequent operation steps outward.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Supplementary Data in Tail of Additional Reference Lines
rules.audit_check: The tail of an additional reference line may be used to specify supplementary process, procedure, or inspection data applying to that welding symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Supplementary data in additional reference line tails is clearly separated and unambiguous.
rules.fail_condition: Additional reference line tails contradict the primary reference line tail without specifying operation scope.
rules.remediation: Clarify which operation each reference line tail governs and resolve conflicting process or specification references.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Weld-All-Around and Field Weld Placement on Each Applicable Reference Line
rules.audit_check: On multiple-reference-line symbols, the weld-all-around (or examine-all-around) symbol SHALL be placed at the junction of the arrow and the reference line for EACH operation to which it applies; the field weld flag may also be placed at each applicable junction.
rules.pass_condition: Every reference line representing an all-around or field operation carries its own all-around circle and/or field flag at its junction with the arrow line.
rules.fail_condition: Only one reference line carries an all-around circle or field flag when subsequent welding or NDE operations on upper reference lines are also required all around or in the field.
rules.remediation: Place the weld-all-around, examine-all-around, and field symbols at the arrow junction of each individual reference line to which they apply.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Field Weld Flag at Right Angle to Reference Line at Arrow Junction
rules.audit_check: A field weld SHALL be specified by a filled flag placed at a right angle (perpendicular) to, and on either side of, the reference line at the junction with the arrow.
rules.pass_condition: Filled field weld flag sits perpendicular to the reference line directly at the arrow-to-reference-line junction.
rules.fail_condition: Field weld flag is placed mid-span on the reference line, at the tail, tilted at an arbitrary angle, or drawn as an unstandardized open triangle.
rules.remediation: Place the standard filled field weld flag perpendicular to the reference line at the arrow junction.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Default Continuous Weld Interpretation Unless Otherwise Indicated
rules.audit_check: Unless otherwise indicated by length/pitch dimensions, hatching, or dimension lines, welding symbols SHALL denote continuous welds.
rules.pass_condition: Omission of weld length is intentional for a continuous weld between abrupt changes in direction.
rules.fail_condition: A partial or intermittent weld is intended (e.g., implied by a note or weight target) but no length/pitch or extent dimensions appear on the symbol or drawing.
rules.remediation: Add explicit length and pitch dimensions (L-P) or extent dimension lines whenever a weld is not intended to be continuous.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Welding Symbols Apply Only Between Abrupt Changes in Direction
rules.audit_check: Welding symbols apply ONLY between abrupt changes in the direction of welding (or to the extent of hatching/dimension lines) unless the weld-all-around symbol is used; additional welding symbols or multiple arrows originating from the single/first reference line SHALL be used for welds across direction changes.
rules.pass_condition: Each straight segment between abrupt corners has its own arrow (from the single/first reference line) or separate symbol, unless a valid weld-all-around symbol applies to all segments identically.
rules.fail_condition: A single arrow points to one side of a multi-segment bracket/gusset with abrupt corners without weld-all-around or additional arrows, leaving adjacent edges unintentionally unwelded; or extra arrows branch from a second reference line instead of the first.
rules.remediation: Add arrows originating from the single/first reference line to every required weld segment, or add separate welding symbols for each direction change.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Specification of Welds on Hidden Members and Auxiliary Views
rules.audit_check: If welding of a hidden member differs from that of a visible member, specific welding information for BOTH members SHALL be specified; if needed for clarification, auxiliary illustrations or views SHALL be provided.
rules.pass_condition: Identical hidden-member welds clearly state applicability (e.g., 'TYPICAL BOTH ANGLES'), and differing hidden-member welds are explicitly detailed in separate symbols and auxiliary/section views.
rules.fail_condition: Hidden member requires different welding from the visible member, or hidden-member welding is obscured with no clarifying view or notation.
rules.remediation: Provide explicit welding symbols for both visible and hidden members and add a clarifying section or auxiliary view.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Partial-Length Weld with Significant Location Must Be Dimensioned
rules.audit_check: A weld having a length less than the available joint length and whose location is functionally significant SHALL have its exact location specified by dimension lines on the drawing.
rules.pass_condition: Partial-length welds in structurally sensitive zones have explicit start/end location dimensions from part edges or datums.
rules.fail_condition: A partial-length weld is called out on a long joint where placement affects structural load path or clearance, but no location dimension is given.
rules.remediation: Add explicit location dimensions on the drawing locating the start and/or end of the partial-length weld.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Partial-Length Weld Without Location Dimension Interpreted as Approximate
rules.audit_check: A partial-length weld specified without location dimensions on the drawing is interpreted as having non-critical (approximate) placement along the joint.
rules.pass_condition: Omission of location dimensions is intentional because the weld may be placed anywhere along the joint.
rules.fail_condition: Design relies on weld placement near a specific corner/load point, yet omits location dimensions so the shop may place it arbitrarily.
rules.remediation: Confirm approximate placement is acceptable; otherwise add explicit drawing dimensions per 5.9.4.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Weld-All-Around Requires Consistent Joint Configuration Around Entire Perimeter
rules.audit_check: When the weld-all-around symbol is placed at the arrow/reference line junction, the weld joint configuration SHALL be consistent with the elements of the welding symbol (same weld type, geometry, and size) at ALL locations where that symbol applies.
rules.pass_condition: Every connected segment around the closed loop has the exact same joint geometry, weld type, and weld size specified by the symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Weld-all-around is applied to a perimeter where joint geometry or weld type changes (e.g., fillet on two sides and flare-bevel-groove on two sides, or interrupted by non-welded gaps/different sizes).
rules.remediation: Remove the weld-all-around symbol and apply separate welding symbols with multiple arrows pointing to each uniform joint configuration.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Circumferential Pipe Welds Excluded From Direction-Change Rule
rules.audit_check: Welds extending continuously around the circumference of a pipe or circular cylinder have no abrupt change in direction and do NOT require the weld-all-around symbol to denote a continuous 360-degree weld.
rules.pass_condition: Continuous circumferential pipe/cylinder weld omits redundant weld-all-around symbol (or if partial, explicitly specifies length/arc extent).
rules.fail_condition: Reviewer or drafter assumes omission of weld-all-around on a pipe butt/socket weld leaves the backside unwelded, or forgets to dimension a partial-arc weld.
rules.remediation: Recognize continuous circumferential interpretation by default; dimension explicit arc lengths or hatching if only partial circumferential welding is desired.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Standard Process Designations (Tables A.2–A.4) and Suffixes (Table A.5) in Tail
rules.audit_check: When specifying a welding, brazing, or allied process in the tail, use the exact letter designation from Annex A Tables A.2–A.4 and, if needed, an optional application suffix from Table A.5 (AD, AU, MA, ME, RO, SA).
rules.pass_condition: Tail process codes match Annex A Tables A.2–A.4 and Table A.5 (e.g., 'GTAW-AU', 'GMAW-P', 'FCAW-G').
rules.fail_condition: Informal shop slang ('MIG', 'TIG', 'STICK', 'MAG', 'HELIARC') or invalid suffixes appear in the welding symbol tail.
rules.remediation: Replace informal process names with standard AWS A2.4 Table A.2–A.4 letter designations and Table A.5 suffixes.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Specifications, Codes, and Procedures in Tail Eliminate Redundant Elements
rules.audit_check: Applicable specifications, codes, WPS numbers, or detail references may be placed in the tail; information already defined in the referenced document need not be repeated in the welding symbol (avoiding conflicting duplicates).
rules.pass_condition: Tail references a valid document/WPS/code ID present on the drawing or project package without conflicting repeated dimensions.
rules.fail_condition: Tail cites a nonexistent spec/note ID or repeats dimensions that contradict the referenced WPS/procedure.
rules.remediation: Ensure every tail reference resolves to an actual code, WPS, or drawing note and remove conflicting duplicated dimensions.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: 'TYPICAL' / 'TYP' Designation Must Completely Identify All Applicable Joints
rules.audit_check: When 'TYPICAL' ('TYP') is placed in the tail of a welding symbol to avoid repetition, the user SHALL provide additional information completely identifying all applicable identical joints (e.g., 'TYP - 5 PLACES', 'TYP 4 PAIR STIFFENERS', 'TYP BOTH FLANGES').
rules.pass_condition: 'TYP' in the tail is accompanied by explicit count and/or unambiguous location scope identifying every identical joint.
rules.fail_condition: Bare 'TYP' or 'TYPICAL' appears in the tail without specifying how many or exactly which joints it governs, or is applied across non-identical joints.
rules.remediation: Qualify every 'TYP' callout with an exact place count and joint description (or reference a specific drawing note), and verify all covered joints are identical.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Special Welds Specified by Cross Section or Detail Referenced in Tail
rules.audit_check: When basic Figure 1 weld symbols are inadequate to depict the required weld (e.g., special joint shapes or skewed joints), the weld SHALL be specified by a cross section, detail, or other data with an explicit reference in the tail of the welding symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Non-standard or complex weld geometry uses an arrow + reference line + tail referencing a fully dimensioned detail/section view on the drawing.
rules.fail_condition: Drafter forces an inaccurate standard weld symbol onto a complex/skewed joint or omits the referenced detail view.
rules.remediation: Provide a fully dimensioned cross-section or detail view of the weld and reference it in the welding symbol tail.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Omission of Empty Tail When No Reference Exists
rules.audit_check: When no specification, process, or other reference is required in the tail, the tail may (and should) be omitted from the welding symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Tail is present only when containing text/references; unused tails are omitted for visual clarity.
rules.fail_condition: An empty tail fork is drawn on the reference line with no text, suggesting accidentally deleted specification data.
rules.remediation: Either populate the required process/specification reference in the tail or remove the empty tail.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: General Drawing Notes Avoid Redundant Welding Symbol Data
rules.audit_check: Drawing notes may specify global welding information (e.g., default fillet size or process) without repeating that information on every individual welding symbol, provided no conflicts exist.
rules.pass_condition: General welding notes are clear, complete, and consistent with individual welding symbols that override them where needed.
rules.fail_condition: General welding note conflicts with individual symbol entries or leaves exceptions ambiguous.
rules.remediation: Ensure general welding notes explicitly state 'UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED' and reconcile any conflicts with individual symbols.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: As-Welded Contours Must Omit Finishing Designators
rules.audit_check: Welds to be made with approximately flush, flat, convex, or concave contours WITHOUT mechanical finishing SHALL include the contour symbol only; finishing designators (C, G, H, M, P, R, U) are NOT to be used when contour is obtained by welding.
rules.pass_condition: As-welded contour requirements show the flush/flat, convex, or concave contour glyph with no finishing method letter.
rules.fail_condition: A finishing designator letter is attached to an as-welded contour symbol, or a note asks for as-welded contour while showing 'G' or 'M'.
rules.remediation: Remove the finishing designator letter when the contour is to be achieved by welding alone.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Finishing Designators Specify Method Only — Not Degree of Surface Finish
rules.audit_check: Postweld finishing designators (C=chipping, G=grinding, H=hammering, M=machining, P=planishing, R=rolling, U=unspecified) specify ONLY the mechanical finishing method and SHALL NOT be used to specify the degree of surface finish (roughness).
rules.pass_condition: Finishing letters are restricted to valid codes (C, G, H, M, P, R, U) paired with a contour symbol, and any required surface roughness (Ra/Rz) is specified via standard surface texture symbols or notes.
rules.fail_condition: Surface roughness values are substituted in the finishing letter slot, invalid finishing letters are used, or a finishing letter appears without a contour symbol.
rules.remediation: Use only valid AWS A2.4 finishing designators (C, G, H, M, P, R, U) with a contour symbol, and specify surface roughness separately per ASME Y14.36.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Letter 'U' Required for Postweld Finishing with Unspecified Method
rules.audit_check: Welds requiring postweld mechanical finishing to an approximately flush, flat, convex, or concave contour with the finishing method unspecified SHALL be indicated by adding the letter 'U' to the contour symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Contour symbol accompanied by 'U' clearly denotes postweld mechanical finishing by any acceptable method.
rules.fail_condition: Drawing requires postweld finishing (method optional) but omits 'U', which under 5.12.1 means as-welded without mechanical finishing.
rules.remediation: Add the finishing designator 'U' above/below the contour symbol whenever mechanical finishing is required by an unspecified method.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Melt-Through Symbol Restricted to One-Sided Welds Requiring CJP Plus Visible Root Reinforcement
rules.audit_check: The melt-through symbol (solid filled semicircle) SHALL be used ONLY when complete joint penetration (CJP) plus visible root reinforcement is required in welds made from ONE side.
rules.pass_condition: Melt-through symbol appears exclusively on single-sided groove or flanged edge welds requiring CJP with visible root reinforcement.
rules.fail_condition: Melt-through symbol is combined with a double-sided groove weld, fillet weld, or partial joint penetration (PJP) groove weld.
rules.remediation: Remove the melt-through symbol on two-sided or PJP welds; use a back/backing weld symbol or omit melt-through if root reinforcement is not required.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Melt-Through Symbol Placed on Side Opposite Weld Symbol
rules.audit_check: The melt-through symbol SHALL be placed on the side of the reference line opposite the weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Solid filled melt-through semicircle sits directly opposite the single-sided weld symbol across the reference line.
rules.fail_condition: Melt-through symbol is drawn on the same side of the reference line as the weld symbol or detached from the reference line.
rules.remediation: Relocate the melt-through symbol to the side of the reference line directly opposite the weld symbol.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Optional Root Reinforcement Height Placed Left of Melt-Through Symbol
rules.audit_check: When a specific height of root reinforcement is required with a melt-through symbol, that dimension is placed to the left of the melt-through symbol (or omitted if unspecified).
rules.pass_condition: Root reinforcement height appears to the left of the melt-through symbol on the melt-through side of the reference line, or is omitted.
rules.fail_condition: Root reinforcement height is placed to the right of the melt-through symbol or on the weld-symbol side where it can be misread as weld size or depth of bevel.
rules.remediation: Place the root reinforcement height dimension strictly to the left of the melt-through symbol.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Melt-Through with Edge Welds on Flanged Butt Joints
rules.audit_check: Edge welds requiring complete joint penetration on flanged butt joints SHALL be specified by the edge weld symbol with the melt-through symbol on the opposite side of the reference line; flange geometry details are part of the drawing and NOT specified by the welding symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Flanged butt joint CJP callout shows edge weld + opposite-side melt-through symbol, with flange height/radius dimensioned on the part view.
rules.fail_condition: Flange dimensions are forced into the welding symbol or melt-through is omitted when CJP is required on a flanged butt joint.
rules.remediation: Specify CJP flanged butt welds using the edge weld symbol plus opposite-side melt-through symbol, and dimension flanges on the part view.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Melt-Through with Edge Welds on Flanged Corner Joints
rules.audit_check: Edge welds requiring complete joint penetration on flanged corner joints SHALL be specified by the edge weld symbol with the melt-through symbol on the opposite side of the reference line; flange details belong on the drawing, not the welding symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Flanged corner joint CJP callout shows edge weld + opposite-side melt-through symbol, with flange geometry dimensioned on the drawing.
rules.fail_condition: Flanged corner CJP edge weld omits the opposite-side melt-through symbol or embeds flange dimensions inside the welding symbol.
rules.remediation: Add the melt-through symbol opposite the edge weld symbol and keep flange dimensions on the part geometry.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Standard Symbol Proportions per Annex B (U.S.) or Annex C (SI)
rules.audit_check: Welding symbols for high-precision drawings or publications SHOULD be drawn using the proportions and angles given in Annex B (U.S. Customary) or Annex C (SI).
rules.pass_condition: Symbols are legible, consistently scaled, and visually distinguishable (e.g., plug vs. edge vs. backing, V vs. bevel).
rules.fail_condition: Badly skewed or squashed weld symbols make it visually ambiguous whether a glyph is a V-groove, bevel-groove, fillet, or backing rectangle.
rules.remediation: Use standardized CAD welding symbol blocks conforming to AWS A2.4 Annex B or Annex C proportions.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Consistent Drawing Units — Dual Units Strictly Prohibited on Welding Symbols
rules.audit_check: The exact same measurement unit system that is standard for the drawing SHALL be used on all welding symbols; dual units (e.g., '1/4 [6.4]') SHALL NOT be used on welding symbols (use a separate conversion table on the drawing if conversions are desired).
rules.pass_condition: Every weld size, root opening, length, and pitch matches the drawing's single governing unit system with no bracketed dual units on the symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Dual units (inch + mm) appear directly on a welding symbol, or a metric drawing contains inch fillet sizes (e.g., 1/4) on weld symbols without unit consistency.
rules.remediation: Remove dual units from all welding symbols, match the drawing's primary unit system, and place any needed unit conversions in a dedicated drawing table.

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Weld Dimension Tolerances Must Explicitly Reference the Governed Dimension
rules.audit_check: When a tolerance applies to a welding symbol dimension (placed in the tail, drawing note, table, code, or specification), an explicit reference MUST be made identifying which specific weld dimension (e.g., 'FILLET SIZE +1/8 -0', 'SEGMENT LENGTH +1/4 -1/4') the tolerance governs.
rules.pass_condition: Every weld tolerance explicitly names the exact dimension it controls (size, length, pitch, root opening, groove angle, etc.).
rules.fail_condition: A bare tolerance such as '±1/16' appears in the tail of a multi-dimension welding symbol (e.g., fillet size + length + pitch) without stating which dimension it controls.
rules.remediation: State the exact weld parameter alongside the tolerance in the tail or referenced note (e.g., 'FILLET SIZE +1/8 -0' or 'SEGMENT LENGTH ±1/4').

rules.section: Clause 5: General Provisions for Welding Symbols
rules.title: Single Reference Line Specifies Pre-Weld Geometry Only — Exclude Post-Operation Geometry Changes
rules.audit_check: A single-reference-line welding symbol specifies ONLY the joint geometry to be established prior to the start of welding; changes in groove geometry resulting from welding operations (such as U-shaped grooves created by backgouging to sound metal) are NOT to be shown as part of the welding symbol.
rules.pass_condition: The weld symbol depicts only the initial pre-weld edge preparation, with backgouging/backing specified via tail note or operation sequence.
rules.fail_condition: A U-groove symbol is placed on the backgouged side solely to represent the shape carved during air-carbon-arc backgouging rather than an initial pre-weld machined U-groove.
rules.remediation: Show only the pre-weld joint preparation on the welding symbol (e.g., square-groove or back weld with 'BACKGOUGE' in the tail) and remove post-backgouge U-groove glyphs.

rules.title: Single-Groove Dimensions Placed on Same Side as Weld Symbol
rules.audit_check: All dimensions of a single-groove weld (depth of bevel S, groove weld size (E), root opening R, groove angle A, length L, pitch P) SHALL be specified on the same side of the reference line as the groove weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Every dimension for an arrow-side single groove is below the reference line, and every dimension for an other-side single groove is above it.
rules.fail_condition: A single-groove weld symbol is on one side of the reference line while its size, angle, root opening, or length is placed on the opposite side.
rules.remediation: Move all dimensions for the single-groove weld onto the same side of the reference line as its weld symbol.

rules.title: Double-Groove Must Dimension Each Groove; Root Opening Shown Once
rules.audit_check: Each groove (arrow side and other side) of a double-groove joint SHALL be individually dimensioned (depth of bevel, weld size, groove angle as applicable); however, the root opening need appear only once.
rules.pass_condition: Both arrow-side and other-side groove symbols carry their respective dimensions (even when symmetrical), while root opening appears inside one side only.
rules.fail_condition: Dimensions are shown on only one side of a double-groove weld symbol assuming the opposite side matches, or root opening is conflictingly repeated on both sides.
rules.remediation: Specify groove depth/size and angle on BOTH sides of the double-groove symbol, and place the root opening once inside one groove symbol.

rules.title: Broken Arrow Identifies Beveled/J-Prepared Member
rules.audit_check: Use a broken arrow pointing to the specific member whenever it is necessary to designate which member receives a single/double bevel-groove or single/double J-groove edge preparation.
rules.pass_condition: Broken arrow points clearly to the exact member to be beveled or J-grooved when both members could otherwise be prepared.
rules.fail_condition: A butt joint between dissimilar thicknesses or materials uses a straight arrow on a bevel/J-groove where preparing the wrong member causes weld failure.
rules.remediation: Break the arrow toward the specific member requiring the bevel or J-groove edge preparation.

rules.title: Straight Arrow on Single-Bevel/Single-J Allows Either Member Preparation
rules.audit_check: A straight (unbroken) arrow on a single-bevel or single-J groove weld in a butt joint means EITHER member may receive the beveled/J edge preparation.
rules.pass_condition: Design truly allows either member to be prepared when a straight arrow is used.
rules.fail_condition: Design requires a specific member to be beveled (e.g., thicker plate or weldment base) but uses a straight arrow.
rules.remediation: Verify either-member preparation is acceptable; otherwise break the arrow toward the required member per 5.4.1.

rules.title: Straight Arrow on Double-Bevel/Double-J Permits Split Member Preparations
rules.audit_check: A straight arrow on a double-bevel or double-J groove weld means either or both members may have the edge shape, including preparing one member on the arrow side and the opposite member on the other side.
rules.pass_condition: All four permissible bevel/J split combinations shown in Clause 6.1.3.3 are functionally acceptable.
rules.fail_condition: A double-bevel butt joint requires both bevels on the same member, yet uses a straight arrow permitting split bevels across opposite plates.
rules.remediation: Use a broken arrow pointing to the specific member if both bevel/J preparations must be machined on that single member.

rules.category: Depth of Bevel & Groove Weld Size
rules.title: Depth of Bevel 'S' and Groove Weld Size '(E)' Placed Left of Symbol
rules.audit_check: When specified, the depth of bevel 'S' and the groove weld size '(E)' SHALL be placed to the left of the groove weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Depth of bevel S and/or parenthesized groove weld size (E) sit immediately to the left of the groove weld glyph on the same side of the reference line.
rules.fail_condition: Depth of bevel or groove weld size is placed to the right, inside, or above/below the groove weld symbol.
rules.remediation: Relocate S and (E) immediately to the left of the groove weld symbol.

rules.category: Depth of Bevel & Groove Weld Size
rules.title: Omission of S and (E) Requires Complete Joint Penetration (CJP)
rules.audit_check: Omitting both depth of bevel S and groove weld size (E) to the left of a groove weld symbol requires a Complete Joint Penetration (CJP) weld extending fully through the joint thickness.
rules.pass_condition: CJP through full joint thickness is genuinely required and feasible (note: high fabrication/inspection cost if unintended).
rules.fail_condition: A non-critical or partial-penetration groove weld omits S and (E), unintentionally forcing expensive CJP welding and NDE.
rules.remediation: Verify CJP is intended; if Partial Joint Penetration (PJP) is desired, specify groove weld size in parentheses (E) per 6.2.3.

rules.category: Depth of Bevel & Groove Weld Size
rules.title: PJP Groove Weld Size Must Be Enclosed in Parentheses '(E)'
rules.audit_check: For Partial Joint Penetration (PJP) groove welds where groove weld size is specified and depth of bevel is not specified, the groove weld size SHALL be enclosed in parentheses '(E)' to the left of the weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: PJP groove weld size is wrapped in parentheses—e.g., '(3/4)' or '(10)'—to the left of the groove symbol.
rules.fail_condition: A PJP groove weld size is placed left of a V/bevel/U/J symbol WITHOUT parentheses (which under 6.2.5/6.2.7 denotes depth of bevel S instead of weld size E).
rules.remediation: Enclose the groove weld size in parentheses '(E)' to the left of the groove weld symbol.

rules.category: Depth of Bevel & Groove Weld Size
rules.title: Nonsymmetrical CJP Double-Groove Weld Sizes Must Be Specified in Parentheses
rules.audit_check: For nonsymmetrical CJP double-groove welds (arrow side vs. other side) where depth of bevel is not specified, the groove weld size of each side SHALL be specified in parentheses '(E)' (note: symmetrical CJP double-groove sizes may optionally be shown in parentheses; total effective weld size cannot exceed plate thickness T).
rules.pass_condition: Nonsymmetrical CJP double-groove symbols show parenthesized sizes on both sides (e.g., '(1/4)' above and '(3/8)' below) whose combined penetration achieves full thickness T.
rules.fail_condition: Nonsymmetrical CJP double-groove omits parentheses or specifies weld sizes on one side only.
rules.remediation: Specify each side's groove weld size in parentheses '(E)' on both sides of the nonsymmetrical double-groove symbol.

rules.category: Depth of Bevel & Groove Weld Size
rules.title: Unparenthesized Left Dimension Denotes Depth of Bevel Only
rules.audit_check: A dimension NOT in parentheses placed to the left of a bevel-, V-, J-, or U-groove weld symbol specifies ONLY the depth of bevel 'S' (requiring groove weld size to be defined elsewhere or governed by 6.2.7).
rules.pass_condition: Unparenthesized dimension represents bevel preparation depth S and any distinct weld size (E) is clearly specified in a referenced spec/WPS or intended as E >= S.
rules.fail_condition: Drafter wrote an unparenthesized number intending to specify weld size E without realizing it governs depth of bevel S.
rules.remediation: Add parenthesized groove weld size as 'S(E)' or replace with '(E)' if only groove weld size is to be controlled.

rules.category: Depth of Bevel & Groove Weld Size
rules.title: Combined 'S(E)' Format; Square-Groove Shows Only '(E)'
visual_syntax_triggers: Depth of Bevel on Square Groove
rules.audit_check: When both depth of bevel and groove weld size are specified, they SHALL appear to the left of the groove symbol as 'S(E)'; for square-groove welds (which have no bevel), ONLY the parenthesized groove weld size '(E)' SHALL be shown.
rules.pass_condition: Bevel/V/U/J/flare grooves use 'S(E)' format, and square-groove welds show only '(E)' (or blank for CJP).
rules.fail_condition: Order is reversed as '(E)S', parentheses are omitted, or an unparenthesized depth of bevel 'S' is placed left of a square-groove weld symbol.
rules.remediation: Format combined groove dimensions as 'S(E)' and remove any depth-of-bevel 'S' value from square-groove weld symbols, retaining only '(E)'.

rules.category: Depth of Bevel & Groove Weld Size
rules.title: Depth of Bevel Without Weld Size Specifies Minimum Weld Size >= S
rules.audit_check: A groove welding symbol with depth of bevel 'S' specified and groove weld size '(E)' neither shown nor specified elsewhere specifies a groove weld size NOT LESS THAN the depth of bevel 'S'.
rules.pass_condition: Intent is truly a minimum weld size E >= S (note: processes like SMAW/FCAW/GMAW with small bevel angles often have effective throat less than S unless qualified).
rules.fail_condition: A narrow bevel angle or process yields weld size less than S, or designer intended E < S (e.g., 7/8 (3/4)) without explicitly specifying '(E)'.
rules.remediation: Explicitly specify 'S(E)' whenever the required groove weld size differs from depth of bevel S.

rules.title: Optional Joint Geometry with CJP Uses 'CJP' in Tail and Omits Weld Symbol
rules.audit_check: Optional joint geometry requiring Complete Joint Penetration SHALL be specified by placing the letters 'CJP' in the tail of the welding symbol and omitting the weld symbol from the reference line.
rules.pass_condition: Reference line has no groove weld glyph and tail contains 'CJP' (optionally accompanied by code/WPS reference).
rules.fail_condition: 'CJP' is placed on the reference line instead of the tail, or a conflicting partial-penetration size '(E)' is combined with 'CJP' in the tail.
rules.remediation: Place 'CJP' in the tail and omit the weld symbol when joint geometry is optional (or use a specific groove symbol without S/(E) if geometry is fixed).

rules.title: Optional Joint Geometry with Specified Groove Weld Size Uses '(E)' Without Weld Symbol
rules.audit_check: Optional joint geometry with a specified groove weld size (PJP) SHALL be specified by placing the parenthesized dimension '(E)' on the arrow side and/or other side of the reference line while omitting the weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Parenthesized size '(E)' sits below and/or above the reference line with no weld glyph when groove type is left optional to the fabricator.
rules.fail_condition: Dimension is placed without parentheses on a bare reference line, making it ambiguous whether it is a note or groove weld size.
rules.remediation: Enclose the required groove weld size in parentheses '(E)' on the applicable side(s) of the bare reference line.

rules.title: Dimension 'S' of Flare-Groove Welds Extends Only to Tangent Point
rules.audit_check: For flare-bevel-groove and flare-V-groove welds, dimension 'S' extends ONLY from the outer surface to the tangent point of the curved member (equal to outside bend radius or round bar radius).
rules.pass_condition: Specified 'S' matches the curved member's radius to the tangent point and specified '(E)' is a physically achievable fraction of that radius.
rules.fail_condition: 'S' exceeds the actual bend/bar radius, or '(E)' exceeds 'S' without a reinforcing fillet weld symbol.
rules.remediation: Set 'S' equal to the distance to the tangent point (bend/bar radius) and verify '(E)' is achievable per the governing welding code (see Annex D6.2.10).

rules.title: Root Opening Placed Inside Weld Symbol on One Side Only
rules.audit_check: The root opening 'R' of groove welds SHALL be specified inside the weld symbol and ONLY on one side of the reference line (never duplicated on both sides of a double-groove symbol).
rules.pass_condition: Root opening value (including '0' when zero gap is mandated) sits inside the groove glyph on one side of the reference line only.
rules.fail_condition: Root opening is placed outside the groove symbol, to the left/right, or repeated on both sides of a double-groove symbol.
rules.remediation: Place the root opening dimension inside the groove weld symbol on one side of the reference line only.

rules.title: Groove Angle Placed Outside Weld Symbol
rules.audit_check: The groove angle (included angle of V/U or bevel angle of bevel/J) SHALL be specified outside the weld symbol (above for other side, below for arrow side) in degrees.
rules.pass_condition: Groove angle with degree symbol (e.g., 45°, 60°) sits cleanly outside the open mouth of the groove weld symbol on each grooved side.
rules.fail_condition: Groove angle is squeezed inside the weld symbol (where root opening belongs), lacks a degree symbol, or is omitted on one side of a double-groove.
rules.remediation: Place the groove angle in degrees outside the groove weld symbol for every grooved side.

rules.title: Groove Radii and Root Faces of U- and J-Grooves Must Reference Cross Section/Detail
rules.audit_check: The groove radii and root faces of U-groove and J-groove welds SHALL be specified by a cross section, detail, or other data (such as a prequalified WPS/joint table) with an explicit reference thereto in the tail of the welding symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Every U- or J-groove symbol includes a tail reference to a dimensioned detail/section or qualified joint specification defining groove radius and root face.
rules.fail_condition: A U-groove or J-groove weld symbol is shown without any tail reference to groove radius or root face geometry, leaving machining geometry undefined.
rules.remediation: Add a dimensioned groove cross-section detail (or qualified WPS joint designation) and reference it in the tail of the U- or J-groove welding symbol.

rules.title: Length of Groove Weld Placed Right of Weld Symbol
rules.audit_check: When indicated on the welding symbol, the length of a groove weld SHALL be specified to the right of the groove weld symbol on the same side of the reference line.
rules.pass_condition: Groove weld length sits immediately to the right of the groove weld glyph.
rules.fail_condition: Groove weld length is placed to the left of the symbol or in the tail.
rules.remediation: Move the groove weld length dimension to the right of the groove weld symbol.

rules.title: Omission of Length Indicates Full Joint Length Groove Weld
rules.audit_check: When no length dimension is specified to the right of a groove weld symbol, the groove weld extends for the full length of the joint (between abrupt changes in direction).
rules.pass_condition: Full-length groove welding is intended when length is omitted.
rules.fail_condition: Only a partial groove weld length is intended, yet no length dimension or extent lines are provided.
rules.remediation: Add the required length dimension to the right of the groove weld symbol (and location dimensions if placement is critical).

rules.title: Specific Groove Weld Lengths and Locations via Dimension Lines
rules.audit_check: Specific groove weld lengths and exact positions along a joint may be specified by combining the welding symbol with extension and dimension lines on the drawing.
rules.pass_condition: Dimension lines clearly bound the groove weld segment and match the length shown on the welding symbol (no conflicting numbers).
rules.fail_condition: Length shown in dimension lines conflicts with length written to the right of the groove weld symbol.
rules.remediation: Reconcile the drawing dimension lines and the length value on the welding symbol.

rules.title: Graphical Hatching Allowed to Depict Groove Weld Extent
rules.audit_check: Hatching along the joint line may be used to graphically depict the extent of groove welds in conjunction with dimension lines and welding symbols.
rules.pass_condition: Hatched weld zones align with arrow terminations and extent dimensions.
rules.fail_condition: Hatched weld zones contradict the welding symbol length or omit bounding dimensions where exact placement is needed.
rules.remediation: Align weld hatching cleanly with the welding symbol arrows and extent dimension lines.

rules.title: Groove Welds with Direction Changes Must Follow Clause 5.9.2
rules.audit_check: Symbols for groove welds involving abrupt changes in welding direction SHALL comply with 5.9.2 (separate arrows from the first reference line, separate symbols for differing weld types such as fillet vs. flare-bevel, or valid weld-all-around only where uniform).
rules.pass_condition: Each direction segment is explicitly addressed by multiple arrows or separate symbols when weld geometry changes.
rules.fail_condition: Single groove arrow stops at a corner leaving perpendicular legs unspecified, or weld-all-around mixes fillet and flare-bevel grooves.
rules.remediation: Add separate arrows or separate welding symbols for each direction change per 5.9.2 and D5.9.2.

rules.title: Intermittent Groove Weld Pitch Defined as Center-to-Center Distance
rules.audit_check: The pitch 'P' of intermittent groove welds SHALL be defined as the center-to-center distance between adjacent weld segments on one side of the joint (NOT clear gap; hence pitch P must exceed segment length L).
rules.pass_condition: Pitch P is strictly greater than segment length L and represents center-to-center spacing on one side.
rules.fail_condition: Pitch P is less than or equal to segment length L (indicating drafter mistakenly entered clear gap instead of center-to-center pitch).
rules.remediation: Convert clear gap to center-to-center pitch (P = length L + clear gap) so P > L.

rules.title: Intermittent Groove Weld Pitch Placed Right of Length After Hyphen
rules.audit_check: The pitch of intermittent groove welds SHALL be specified to the right of the length dimension separated by a hyphen ('L-P', e.g., '4-8' or '125-200').
rules.pass_condition: Intermittent groove callout uses exact 'L-P' format to the right of the groove weld symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Length and pitch use '@' or '/' (e.g., '4 @ 8'), omit the hyphen, or appear in reverse order.
rules.remediation: Format intermittent groove length and pitch strictly as 'L-P' to the right of the weld symbol.

rules.title: Chain Intermittent Groove Welds Dimensioned on Both Sides (Aligned)
rules.audit_check: Dimensions of chain intermittent groove welds SHALL be specified on BOTH sides of the reference line with weld symbols directly aligned across the reference line (indicating segments approximately opposite one another).
rules.pass_condition: Aligned groove symbols on both sides each carry their 'L-P' dimensions.
rules.fail_condition: Chain intermittent groove shows 'L-P' on only one side of a both-sides symbol.
rules.remediation: Specify length-pitch 'L-P' on both sides of the reference line with aligned groove weld symbols.

rules.title: Staggered Intermittent Groove Welds Offset Across Reference Line
rules.audit_check: Dimensions of staggered intermittent groove welds SHALL be specified on BOTH sides of the reference line, and the arrow-side and other-side groove weld symbols SHALL be horizontally offset across the reference line (denoting symmetric staggered spacing).
rules.pass_condition: Top and bottom groove symbols are visibly offset horizontally and both carry 'L-P' dimensions.
rules.fail_condition: Drawing notes 'STAGGERED' in tail while symbols remain vertically aligned, or 'L-P' is missing on one side.
rules.remediation: Horizontally offset the arrow-side and other-side groove weld symbols across the reference line and specify 'L-P' on both sides.

rules.title: Extent and End Segments of Intermittent Groove Welds
rules.audit_check: Additional groove weld lengths intended at the ends of an intermittent joint SHALL be specified by separate welding symbols and dimensioned on the drawing; when no end welds are intended, unwelded end lengths SHOULD NOT exceed the clear distance between segments and should be dimensioned.
rules.pass_condition: End weld segments use separate symbols + dimensions, or unwelded end margins are dimensioned and <= clear spacing (P - L).
rules.fail_condition: Required end welds are omitted from symbols, or unwelded end margins exceed the clear space between segments without justification.
rules.remediation: Add separate welding symbols and dimensions for end segments, or dimension unwelded end margins <= (P - L).

rules.title: Explicit Location Required When Intermittent Groove Placement Is Not Obvious
rules.audit_check: When the location of intermittent groove welds is not obvious (such as on a circular or curved joint), specific segment locations SHALL be provided using dimension lines or graphical hatching.
rules.pass_condition: Circular or complex intermittent groove joints show explicit angular/linear segment location dimensions or hatching.
rules.fail_condition: Intermittent groove weld symbol is pointed at a circular joint with no start point, angular spacing, or hatching.
rules.remediation: Locate intermittent segments explicitly with dimension lines or hatching on the drawing.

rules.title: As-Welded Groove Weld Contours (Flush or Convex Only)
rules.audit_check: Groove welds to be made with approximately flush or convex faces without postweld finishing SHALL be specified by adding the flush or convex contour symbol without a finishing designator.
rules.pass_condition: Flush or convex contour symbol appears outside the groove symbol with no finishing letter.
rules.fail_condition: Concave contour is improperly applied to a groove weld or a finishing letter is added to an as-welded callout.
rules.remediation: Use only flush or convex contour symbols on groove welds and omit finishing letters for as-welded contours.

rules.title: Postweld-Finished Groove Contours and Flat-Not-Flush Tail Note
rules.audit_check: Groove welds finished flush or convex by postweld finishing SHALL include BOTH the contour symbol and a finishing designator (C, G, H, M, P, R, U); welds requiring a flat but NOT flush face SHALL include an explanatory note in the tail (e.g., 'GRIND FACE FLAT').
rules.pass_condition: Postweld-finished groove welds carry both contour + finishing letter, and flat-above-base-metal requirements include an explicit tail note.
rules.fail_condition: Finishing letter appears without contour symbol, or flat-but-not-flush reinforcement is demanded using only a bare flush line without tail clarification.
rules.remediation: Pair the contour symbol with the finishing letter and add an explanatory tail note whenever a flat (non-flush) face is required.

rules.title: Back vs. Backing Weld Distinguished Strictly by Sequence
rules.audit_check: The back weld and backing weld symbols are graphically identical (open semicircle); sequence determines designation—a back weld is deposited AFTER the groove weld, while a backing weld is deposited BEFORE the groove weld.
rules.pass_condition: Sequence is unambiguously declared via tail text or multiple reference lines.
rules.fail_condition: An open semicircle appears opposite a groove weld on a single reference line with NO tail note and NO second reference line, making it impossible to tell if it is a back weld or backing weld.
rules.remediation: Specify 'BACK WELD' or 'BACKING WELD' in the tail, or separate operations onto sequenced multiple reference lines per 6.7.2/6.7.3.

rules.title: Back Weld Specification via Tail Note or Subsequent Reference Line
rules.audit_check: Placed opposite a groove weld symbol, a back weld SHALL either state 'BACK WELD' in the tail (single reference line) OR appear on a reference line subsequent to (farther from the arrow than) the groove weld reference line.
rules.pass_condition: Back weld uses 'BACK WELD' in tail on a single reference line, or sits on the 2nd reference line farther from the arrow than the 1st-line groove weld.
rules.fail_condition: Back weld lacks 'BACK WELD' in the tail on a single reference line, or is placed closer to the arrow than the groove weld (which specifies a backing weld instead).
rules.remediation: Add 'BACK WELD' to the tail on a single reference line, or move the back weld symbol onto a subsequent reference line farther from the arrow.

rules.title: Backing Weld Specification via Tail Note or Prior Reference Line
rules.audit_check: Placed opposite a groove weld symbol, a backing weld SHALL either state 'BACKING WELD' in the tail (single reference line) OR appear on a reference line prior to (closer to the arrow than) the groove weld reference line.
rules.pass_condition: Backing weld uses 'BACKING WELD' in tail on a single reference line, or sits on the 1st reference line nearer the arrow than the 2nd-line groove weld.
rules.fail_condition: Backing weld lacks 'BACKING WELD' in the tail on a single reference line, or is placed farther from the arrow than the groove weld.
rules.remediation: Add 'BACKING WELD' to the tail on a single reference line, or place the backing weld on the prior reference line nearest the arrow.

rules.title: As-Welded Contours of Back or Backing Welds
rules.audit_check: Back or backing welds to be welded approximately flush or convex without postweld finishing SHALL include the flush or convex contour symbol without a finishing designator.
rules.pass_condition: Flush or convex contour glyph is placed outside the back/backing weld semicircle with no finishing letter.
rules.fail_condition: Finishing letter is added to an as-welded back/backing weld contour.
rules.remediation: Omit finishing letters when back/backing weld contour is to be achieved as-welded.

rules.title: Postweld-Finished Contours of Back or Backing Welds
rules.audit_check: Back or backing welds finished flush or convex by postweld finishing SHALL carry both contour symbol and finishing designator; flat-but-not-flush surfaces require an explanatory note in the tail.
rules.pass_condition: Both contour symbol and finishing designator appear on the back/backing symbol, with a tail note if flat-but-not-flush.
rules.fail_condition: Finishing letter appears without contour symbol, or flat-not-flush requirement lacks a tail note.
rules.remediation: Include both contour symbol and finishing designator, and add a tail note for flat-but-not-flush requirements.

rules.title: Joints with Backing — Opposite Rectangle, 'R' for Removal, Material & Dimensions
rules.audit_check: A joint with backing SHALL show the rectangular backing symbol opposite the groove weld symbol; if backing is removed after welding, 'R' SHALL be placed inside the rectangle; backing material and dimensions SHALL be specified in the tail or on the drawing.
rules.pass_condition: Backing rectangle sits opposite the groove symbol, includes 'R' if removable, and specifies material grade and cross-section dimensions (e.g., '1/4 x 1 A36') in tail or drawing.
rules.fail_condition: Backing symbol is missing material/size specification, placed on same side as groove, or uses a text note instead of 'R' inside the rectangle for removal.
rules.remediation: Place the backing rectangle opposite the groove weld, insert 'R' inside if removed after welding, and specify backing material and dimensions in the tail or BOM/drawing.

rules.title: Joints with Spacers — Centered Rectangle on Nearest Reference Line, Material & Size
rules.audit_check: A joint with a spacer SHALL modify the groove weld symbol to contain a rectangle centered on the reference line; with multiple reference lines, the spacer rectangle SHALL appear on the reference line nearest the arrow; spacer material and dimensions SHALL be specified in the tail or on the drawing.
rules.pass_condition: Spacer rectangle sits inside the double-groove symbol on the 1st reference line (nearest arrow) with material and dimensions specified in tail or drawing.
rules.fail_condition: Spacer material/dimensions are omitted, spacer rectangle is placed on a later reference line, or backing rectangle is confused with a spacer.
rules.remediation: Draw the spacer rectangle centered within the groove symbol on the reference line nearest the arrow and specify spacer material and dimensions.

rules.title: Consumable Inserts — Opposite Square Symbol and AWS A5.30 Class in Tail
rules.audit_check: Consumable inserts SHALL be specified by placing the square consumable insert symbol on the side of the reference line opposite the groove weld symbol, AND the AWS consumable insert class (per AWS A5.30/A5.30M) SHALL be placed in the tail.
rules.pass_condition: Square insert glyph sits opposite the groove weld symbol and tail states exact AWS insert class (e.g., 'CLASS 1 INSERT', 'CLASS 3 INSERT').
rules.fail_condition: Consumable insert square appears without an AWS A5.30 class in the tail, or a rectangular backing symbol is drawn instead of the square consumable insert glyph.
rules.remediation: Draw the square consumable insert symbol opposite the groove weld and specify the required AWS A5.30/A5.30M insert class in the tail.

rules.title: Backgouging Reference in Tail and Nonsymmetrical Double-Groove Depths
rules.audit_check: Groove welds requiring backgouging SHALL include a reference to backgouging in the tail; for nonsymmetrical double-groove welds, the symbol SHALL show the required depth of groove and groove angle for EACH side (single or symmetrical double-groove welds without a root face may omit depth of groove).
rules.pass_condition: Tail explicitly states 'BACKGOUGE' (or procedure reference), and nonsymmetrical double-groove welds show depth and angle on both sides.
rules.fail_condition: Backgouging is omitted from the tail, or a nonsymmetrical double-groove with backgouging omits the groove depths or angles.
rules.remediation: Add 'BACKGOUGE' in the tail and specify depth of groove and groove angle for both sides on nonsymmetrical double-groove joints.

rules.title: Sealing-Only Welds Specified as 'SEAL WELD' in Tail
rules.audit_check: When the intent of a weld is to fulfill a sealing function only, it SHALL be designated in the tail of the welding symbol as 'SEAL WELD' (paired with appropriate weld type and sizing per Annex D6.12).
rules.pass_condition: Tail states 'SEAL WELD' alongside the required weld symbol and size.
rules.fail_condition: A weld intended solely for fluid/gas sealing is indistinguishable from structural welds, or relies only on a bare 'SEAL WELD' note with no weld type/size.
rules.remediation: Specify 'SEAL WELD' in the tail along with the required weld type and size.

rules.title: Skewed Groove Joints Require Dimensioned Drawing Detail
rules.audit_check: When the angle between fusion faces makes identification of the groove weld type and proper weld symbol questionable, a dimensioned detail of the desired joint and weld configuration SHALL be shown on the drawing (referenced in the tail).
rules.pass_condition: Skewed joint (e.g., 45° or sharper member intersection) uses a welding symbol referencing a fully dimensioned detail view showing leg/throat/root dimensions.
rules.fail_condition: Acute skewed joint relies solely on an unqualified standard groove symbol without a detail view clarifying effective throat and fusion geometry.
rules.remediation: Add a fully dimensioned joint/weld cross-section detail view on the drawing and reference it in the tail.

rules.title: Fillet Weld Dimensions Placed on Same Side as Weld Symbol
rules.audit_check: All dimensions of a fillet weld (size S, length L, pitch P) SHALL be shown on the same side of the reference line as the fillet weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Size, length, and pitch sit on the exact same side (above or below) of the reference line as the fillet triangle.
rules.fail_condition: Fillet dimensions are placed on the opposite side of the reference line from the fillet weld symbol.
rules.remediation: Relocate all fillet weld dimensions to the same side of the reference line as the fillet weld symbol.

rules.title: Double Fillet Welds Must Dimension BOTH Sides Even When Identical
rules.audit_check: For double fillet welds (symbols on both sides of the reference line), the weld dimensions SHALL be specified on BOTH sides of the reference line whether the dimensions are identical or different (unless governed by a general drawing note per 7.1.3).
rules.pass_condition: Both upper and lower fillet weld symbols show their weld size (e.g., '1/2' above and '1/2' below) and length/pitch if applicable.
rules.fail_condition: A double fillet weld symbol specifies size on only one side (e.g., '1/4' below only) expecting the shop to assume the other side is identical.
rules.remediation: Specify the fillet weld size (and length/pitch if applicable) on BOTH the arrow side and the other side of the double fillet symbol.

rules.title: General Drawing Notes May Govern Default Fillet Dimensions
rules.audit_check: Fillet weld dimensions omitted from individual symbols are permissible ONLY when explicitly covered by a general drawing note in accordance with 5.11.6.
rules.pass_condition: Undimensioned fillet symbols are backed by an unambiguous general drawing note specifying default fillet size (e.g., 'ALL FILLET WELDS 1/4 UOS').
rules.fail_condition: Fillet weld symbols omit weld size AND no general drawing note defines a default fillet size, leaving leg size completely unspecified.
rules.remediation: Specify the fillet weld size on the symbol or add an explicit general drawing note defining default fillet weld size.

rules.title: Fillet Weld Size 'S' Placed Left of Fillet Symbol
rules.audit_check: The fillet weld size 'S' (leg length) SHALL be specified to the left of the fillet weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Fillet leg size appears immediately left of the perpendicular leg of the fillet triangle.
rules.fail_condition: Fillet size is placed to the right of the triangle (where length belongs) or enclosed in parentheses.
rules.remediation: Place the fillet weld leg size 'S' immediately to the left of the fillet weld symbol without parentheses.

rules.title: Unequal-Leg Fillet Welds Require Drawing Orientation Clarification
rules.audit_check: Unequal-leg fillet weld sizes SHALL be placed to the left of the fillet symbol (e.g., '1/4 x 3/8'); because the welding symbol does NOT specify leg orientation, the orientation of the legs SHALL be explicitly shown on the drawing (via detail, note, or member thickness constraint).
rules.pass_condition: Unequal fillet callout 'a x b' is paired with an explicit drawing detail, note (e.g., '1/2 LEG ON MEMBER B'), or unambiguous thickness geometry identifying which member receives each leg.
rules.fail_condition: Unequal fillet size 'a x b' appears on a welding symbol with no drawing detail or note indicating which leg goes on the horizontal vs. vertical member.
rules.remediation: Clarify unequal fillet leg orientation directly on the drawing via a cross-section detail or explicit note naming the member for each leg.

rules.title: Fillet Weld Length Placed Right of Fillet Symbol
rules.audit_check: When indicated on the welding symbol, the length of a fillet weld SHALL be specified to the right of the fillet weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Fillet weld length appears immediately to the right of the fillet weld symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Fillet weld length is placed to the left of the symbol or in the tail.
rules.remediation: Move the fillet weld length dimension to the right of the fillet weld symbol.

rules.title: Omission of Fillet Length Denotes Full Joint Length
rules.audit_check: When a fillet weld extends for the full length of the joint between abrupt direction changes, no length dimension need be specified on the welding symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Omission of length intentionally specifies a continuous full-length fillet weld.
rules.fail_condition: Partial fillet length is intended without specifying a length dimension.
rules.remediation: Add the required length dimension to the right of the fillet symbol if full-length welding is not intended.

rules.title: Specific Fillet Lengths and Locations via Dimension Lines
rules.audit_check: Specific lengths and locations of partial fillet welds may be defined by combining the welding symbol with dimension lines on the drawing.
