rules.pass_condition: Dimension lines cleanly locate the fillet segment and agree with the length on the welding symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Drawing dimension lines contradict the length value on the fillet weld symbol.
rules.remediation: Reconcile the fillet weld length on the symbol with the drawing extent dimension lines.

rules.title: Hatching May Graphically Depict Fillet Weld Extent
rules.audit_check: Hatching may be used along joint lines to graphically depict the extent of fillet welds in conjunction with welding symbols and dimensions.
rules.pass_condition: Hatched fillet zones match the symbol arrows and bounding dimension lines.
rules.fail_condition: Hatching conflicts with the symbol length or leaves transitions between different fillet sizes undimensioned.
rules.remediation: Dimension every hatched zone boundary clearly and align arrows to each distinct fillet size.

rules.title: Fillet Welds with Direction Changes Must Follow Clause 5.9.2
rules.audit_check: Symbols for fillet welds involving abrupt changes in welding direction SHALL follow 5.9.2 (multiple arrows from single/first reference line, separate symbols, or valid weld-all-around).
rules.pass_condition: Each fillet segment around abrupt direction changes is explicitly pointed to or covered by a valid uniform weld-all-around symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Fillet weld arrow points to only one edge of a multi-edge bracket without multiple arrows or weld-all-around.
rules.remediation: Add arrows from the reference line to each welded edge or apply a valid weld-all-around symbol if all segments are identical.

rules.title: Intermittent Fillet Weld Pitch Defined as Center-to-Center Distance
rules.audit_check: The pitch 'P' of intermittent fillet welds SHALL be the center-to-center distance between adjacent weld segments on one side of the joint (hence P must exceed segment length L).
rules.pass_condition: Pitch P > segment length L and represents center-to-center spacing on one side.
rules.fail_condition: Pitch P <= segment length L (indicating clear spacing was erroneously entered instead of center-to-center pitch).
rules.remediation: Specify pitch as center-to-center distance (P = length L + clear gap) so P > L.

rules.title: Intermittent Fillet Pitch Placed Right of Length After Hyphen
rules.audit_check: The pitch of intermittent fillet welds SHALL be specified to the right of the length dimension following a hyphen ('L-P', e.g., '2-5' or '75-200').
rules.pass_condition: Length and pitch are formatted as 'L-P' to the right of the fillet weld symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Non-standard separators ('2 @ 5', '2/5', '2x5') or reversed order are used.
rules.remediation: Format intermittent fillet weld length and pitch strictly as 'L-P' to the right of the fillet symbol.

rules.title: Chain Intermittent Fillet Welds Dimensioned on Both Sides (Aligned)
rules.audit_check: Dimensions of chain intermittent fillet welds SHALL be specified on BOTH sides of the reference line, with aligned fillet symbols denoting segments directly opposite one another across the joint.
rules.pass_condition: Left legs of upper and lower fillet triangles align vertically, and both sides display size and 'L-P'.
rules.fail_condition: Dimensions are omitted on one side of a chain intermittent fillet weld symbol.
rules.remediation: Specify size and 'L-P' on both sides of the reference line with vertically aligned fillet triangles.

rules.title: Staggered Intermittent Fillet Welds Offset Across Reference Line
rules.audit_check: Dimensions of staggered intermittent fillet welds SHALL be specified on BOTH sides of the reference line, and the fillet weld symbols SHALL be horizontally offset on opposite sides of the reference line to indicate symmetrically staggered spacing.
rules.pass_condition: Upper and lower fillet triangles are visibly offset horizontally and both sides show size and 'L-P'.
rules.fail_condition: Staggered fillet welding is requested via note while triangles are vertically aligned, or dimensions appear on only one side.
rules.remediation: Offset the upper and lower fillet weld symbols horizontally across the reference line and specify size and 'L-P' on both sides.

rules.title: Intermittent Fillet End Segments and Unwelded End Margins
rules.audit_check: Additional fillet weld lengths intended at the ends of an intermittent joint SHALL be specified by separate welding symbols and dimensioned on the drawing; when no end welds are intended, unwelded end lengths SHOULD NOT exceed the clear distance between segments and should be dimensioned.
rules.pass_condition: End fillet segments have separate symbols and dimensions, or unwelded end margins are dimensioned and <= (P - L).
rules.fail_condition: End segments are omitted or unwelded ends are undimensioned/excessively long.
rules.remediation: Specify end fillet segments with separate symbols and dimensions, or dimension unwelded end margins <= (P - L).

rules.title: Explicit Location Required for Non-Obvious Intermittent Fillet Welds
rules.audit_check: When intermittent fillet weld locations are not obvious (e.g., on circular joints), specific segment locations SHALL be provided via dimension lines or hatching.
rules.pass_condition: Segment locations on circular or irregular joints are explicitly dimensioned or hatched.
rules.fail_condition: Intermittent fillet callout on a circular weld provides no angular or linear location dimensions.
rules.remediation: Locate intermittent fillet segments using dimension lines or graphical hatching.

rules.category: Fillet Welds in Holes and Slots
rules.title: Fillet Welds Inside Holes and Slots Must Use Fillet Weld Symbols
rules.audit_check: Fillet welds deposited around the interior perimeter of holes or slots SHALL be specified using fillet weld symbols (typically with weld-all-around if continuous around the hole/slot), NEVER plug or slot weld symbols.
rules.pass_condition: Interior hole/slot fillet weld uses a fillet weld symbol pointing to the hole/slot edge with fillet leg size.
rules.fail_condition: Plug or slot weld symbol is used when only an interior perimeter fillet weld (not filling the hole/slot) is desired.
rules.remediation: Replace the plug/slot weld symbol with a fillet weld symbol (plus weld-all-around if continuous) and specify fillet size.

rules.title: As-Welded Fillet Contours (Flat, Convex, or Concave)
rules.audit_check: Fillet welds to be made approximately flat, convex, or concave without postweld finishing SHALL include the flat, convex, or concave contour symbol with NO finishing designator.
rules.pass_condition: Contour symbol lies parallel to the hypotenuse of the fillet triangle with no finishing letter.
rules.fail_condition: Finishing letter is attached to an as-welded fillet contour symbol.
rules.remediation: Omit finishing designators when the fillet contour is to be obtained by welding alone.

rules.title: Postweld-Finished Fillet Contours Require Both Contour and Finishing Designator
rules.audit_check: Fillet welds to be finished approximately flat, convex, or concave by postweld finishing SHALL carry BOTH the appropriate contour symbol and finishing designator (C, G, H, M, P, R, or U).
rules.pass_condition: Contour symbol and valid finishing designator both appear along the fillet hypotenuse.
rules.fail_condition: Finishing letter appears without a contour symbol, or an invalid finishing letter is used.
rules.remediation: Include both the contour glyph and valid finishing designator (C, G, H, M, P, R, or U) on the fillet weld symbol.

rules.title: Skewed Fillet Joints Require Dimensioned Detail on Drawing
rules.audit_check: When the angle between fusion faces of a skewed joint makes weld type identification and symbol validity questionable, the detail of the desired joint and weld configuration SHALL be shown on the drawing.
rules.pass_condition: Skewed T- or corner joint references a fully dimensioned detail view specifying required legs/effective throat.
rules.fail_condition: Extreme acute/obtuse skewed joint relies on a plain fillet symbol without detailing required weld profile or effective throat.
rules.remediation: Show a fully dimensioned joint/weld detail on the drawing and reference it in the welding symbol tail.

rules.title: Arrow-Side Plug Weld Symbol Placement
rules.audit_check: Holes in the arrow-side member of a joint for plug welding SHALL be indicated by placing the rectangular plug weld symbol below the reference line.
rules.pass_condition: When the hole is prepared in the arrow-side member, the plug weld symbol is placed below and in direct contact with the reference line.
rules.fail_condition: Arrow-side plug weld hole is shown with the plug weld symbol placed above or centered on the reference line.
rules.remediation: Place the plug weld symbol below the reference line whenever the plug hole is in the arrow-side member.

rules.title: Other-Side Plug Weld Symbol Placement
rules.audit_check: Holes in the other-side member of a joint for plug welding SHALL be indicated by placing the rectangular plug weld symbol above the reference line.
rules.pass_condition: When the hole is prepared in the other-side member, the plug weld symbol is placed above and in direct contact with the reference line.
rules.fail_condition: Other-side plug weld hole is indicated with the symbol below or centered on the reference line.
rules.remediation: Place the plug weld symbol above the reference line whenever the plug hole is located in the other-side member.

rules.title: Plug Weld Dimensions on Same Side as Weld Symbol
rules.audit_check: Dimensions of plug welds SHALL be shown on the same side of the reference line as the plug weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Diameter, countersink angle, depth of filling, pitch, and weld count all appear on the same side of the reference line as the plug weld symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Any plug weld dimension (size, angle, pitch, or count) is placed on the opposite side of the reference line from the plug weld symbol.
rules.remediation: Move all plug weld dimensions to the same side of the reference line as the plug weld symbol.

rules.title: Prohibition of Plug Weld Symbol for Fillet Welds in Holes
rules.audit_check: The plug weld symbol SHALL NOT be used to designate fillet welds inside circular holes; fillet welds in holes SHALL be specified using the fillet weld symbol per Clause 7.5.
rules.pass_condition: Circular holes requiring only perimeter fillet welding use a fillet weld symbol (with weld-all-around if full perimeter), while plug weld symbols are reserved solely for plug welds.
rules.fail_condition: Plug weld symbol is used on a drawing where notes, section views, or joint callouts specify a fillet weld around the inside perimeter of a hole.
rules.remediation: Replace the plug weld symbol with a fillet weld symbol (plus weld-all-around symbol when full-perimeter) in accordance with Clause 7.5.

rules.title: Plug Weld Size (Faying-Surface Diameter with Ø Prefix) Left of Symbol
rules.audit_check: The size of a plug weld (the diameter of the hole at the faying surface) SHALL be shown to the left of the plug weld symbol and SHALL be preceded by the diameter symbol (Ø).
rules.pass_condition: Plug weld diameter at the faying surface appears immediately to the left of the plug weld symbol with a leading Ø symbol (e.g., Ø1/2 or Ø12).
rules.fail_condition: Plug weld size omits the Ø prefix, is placed to the right or inside the symbol, or specifies the outer countersunk top diameter instead of the faying-surface diameter.
rules.remediation: Specify the hole diameter at the faying surface preceded by Ø to the left of the plug weld symbol.

rules.title: Included Angle of Countersink Above or Below Plug Weld Symbol
rules.audit_check: The included angle of countersink of plug welds SHALL be located on the same side of the reference line as the weld symbol, positioned directly below (arrow side) or above (other side) the plug weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Included countersink angle (e.g., 45°, 60°) is placed directly below an arrow-side plug symbol or directly above an other-side plug symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Countersink angle is placed inside the plug symbol, to the left/right of the symbol, or shown as a half-angle rather than the included angle.
rules.remediation: Place the included countersink angle directly below (arrow side) or above (other side) the plug weld symbol on the same side of the reference line.

rules.title: Partial Depth of Filling Specified Inside Plug Weld Symbol
rules.audit_check: When depth of filling of a plug weld is less than complete, the depth of filling SHALL be specified in inches or millimeters inside the plug weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Partial-fill plug weld displays the numeric fill depth cleanly centered inside the rectangular plug weld symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Partial depth of filling is placed outside the plug weld symbol (e.g., to the left or right) or described only by an ambiguous note.
rules.remediation: Place the partial depth of filling value inside the rectangular plug weld symbol using the drawing's unit system.

rules.title: Omission of Depth of Filling Defaults to Complete Filling
rules.audit_check: Omission of a depth-of-filling dimension inside the plug weld symbol specifies complete filling of the hole to the full thickness of the holed member.
rules.pass_condition: Complete filling is genuinely intended whenever the interior of the plug weld symbol is left blank, and no contradictory section view shows partial filling.
rules.fail_condition: Plug weld symbol interior is left blank while a section view, note, or clearance requirement implies partial filling of the hole.
rules.remediation: Confirm whether complete filling is intended; if partial fill is required, enter the exact depth of filling inside the plug weld symbol.

rules.title: Plug Weld Straight-Line Pitch Right of Symbol vs. Non-Linear Spacing on Drawing
rules.audit_check: The pitch (center-to-center spacing) of plug welds in a straight line SHALL be shown to the right of the plug weld symbol; spacing of plug welds not in a straight line SHALL be dimensioned directly on the drawing.
rules.pass_condition: Straight-line plug weld center-to-center pitch is placed immediately to the right of the plug weld symbol, and staggered/curved/grid plug layouts are explicitly dimensioned on the drawing views.
rules.fail_condition: Straight-line pitch is placed to the left of the symbol, edge-to-edge spacing is given instead of center-to-center pitch, or non-linear plug patterns rely solely on a single pitch number in the symbol.
rules.remediation: Place straight-line center-to-center pitch to the right of the plug weld symbol and dimension any non-linear or pattern spacing directly on the drawing views.

rules.title: Number of Plug Welds Specified in Parentheses
rules.audit_check: When a definite number of plug welds is desired in a joint, the number SHALL be shown in parentheses on the same side of the reference line as the weld symbol—above or below the symbol, or above/below the included countersink angle when one is specified.
rules.pass_condition: Plug weld count appears enclosed in parentheses (e.g., (4)) on the same side as the plug symbol, stacked outside any countersink angle.
rules.fail_condition: Weld count is written without parentheses (e.g., 4X), placed in the tail as an ad-hoc note, placed on the opposite side of the reference line, or collides with the countersink angle.
rules.remediation: Specify the definite plug weld count in parentheses (N) on the same side of the reference line above/below the plug symbol (and outside the countersink angle if present).

rules.title: As-Welded Flush or Convex Contour on Plug Welds
rules.audit_check: Plug welds to be welded approximately flush or convex without subsequent mechanical finishing SHALL be specified by adding the flush or convex contour symbol to the welding symbol without a finishing designator.
rules.pass_condition: As-welded flush or convex plug weld displays only the contour symbol above/below the plug weld symbol with no finishing letter.
rules.fail_condition: As-welded contour is requested using prose text instead of the contour symbol, or an unintended finishing letter is attached.
rules.remediation: Add the flush or convex contour symbol (without a finishing designator) to the plug weld symbol.

rules.title: Postweld-Finished Plug Weld Contour and Flat-Not-Flush Note
visual_syntax_triggers: C G H M P R U
rules.audit_check: Plug welds to be made flush or convex by mechanical means SHALL show both the contour symbol and the user's standard finishing letter (C, G, H, M, P, R, or U); plug welds having a flat but not flush surface SHALL include an explanatory note in the tail.
rules.pass_condition: Mechanically finished plug welds combine the contour symbol with a valid finishing letter (C, G, H, M, P, R, U), and any flat-but-not-flush requirement is explicitly explained in the tail.
rules.fail_condition: A finishing letter appears without a contour symbol, an invalid finishing letter is used, or a flat-not-flush surface lacks a clarifying tail note.
rules.remediation: Pair the flush or convex contour symbol with the appropriate finishing letter (C, G, H, M, P, R, or U) and add a tail note whenever 'flat but not flush' is intended.

rules.title: Mandatory Section View for Plug Welds Joining Three or More Members
rules.audit_check: For plug weld joints involving three or more members, a section view of the joint SHALL be provided on the drawing to clearly identify which members have holes and which members require weld penetration.
rules.pass_condition: Every plug weld joint with 3+ stacked members includes a dedicated section view unambiguously depicting hole locations and required penetration across members.
rules.fail_condition: A plug weld symbol is applied to a stack of three or more members without a section view showing which plates are perforated and fused.
rules.remediation: Add a clear section view of the multi-member plug weld joint showing exact hole locations and member penetration.

rules.title: Arrow-Side Slot Weld Symbol Placement
rules.audit_check: Slots in the arrow-side member of a joint for slot welding SHALL be indicated by placing the slot weld symbol below the reference line.
rules.pass_condition: Arrow-side slot weld displays the rectangular slot weld symbol below and touching the reference line.
rules.fail_condition: Arrow-side slot is indicated with the slot weld symbol above or centered on the reference line.
rules.remediation: Place the slot weld symbol below the reference line when the slot is cut in the arrow-side member.

rules.title: Other-Side Slot Weld Symbol Placement
rules.audit_check: Slots in the other-side member of a joint for slot welding SHALL be indicated by placing the slot weld symbol above the reference line.
rules.pass_condition: Other-side slot weld displays the rectangular slot weld symbol above and touching the reference line.
rules.fail_condition: Other-side slot is indicated with the slot weld symbol below or centered on the reference line.
rules.remediation: Place the slot weld symbol above the reference line when the slot is cut in the other-side member.

rules.title: Slot Weld Dimensions on Same Side as Weld Symbol
rules.audit_check: Dimensions of slot welds SHALL be shown on the same side of the reference line as the slot weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Slot width, length, pitch, countersink angle, depth of filling, and count all appear on the same side of the reference line as the slot weld symbol.
rules.fail_condition: One or more slot weld dimensions are placed on the opposite side of the reference line from the slot weld symbol.
rules.remediation: Move all slot weld dimensions to the same side of the reference line as the slot weld symbol.

rules.title: Prohibition of Slot Weld Symbol for Fillet Welds in Slots
rules.audit_check: The slot weld symbol SHALL NOT be used to specify fillet welds inside slots; fillet welds in slots SHALL be designated using the fillet weld symbol per Clause 7.5.
rules.pass_condition: Perimeter fillet welds inside elongated slots are called out with a fillet weld symbol (and weld-all-around when applicable), never a slot weld symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Slot weld symbol is used where the design calls for fillet welding around the inside perimeter of a slot rather than filling the slot.
rules.remediation: Replace the slot weld symbol with a fillet weld symbol in accordance with Clause 7.5.

rules.title: Slot Weld Width (Minor Axis at Faying Surface) Left of Symbol Without Ø
rules.audit_check: The width of a slot weld (dimension of the slot in the direction of the minor axis at the faying surface) SHALL be shown to the left of the slot weld symbol without a diameter symbol (Ø).
rules.pass_condition: Slot width at the faying surface appears immediately to the left of the slot weld symbol as a plain linear dimension with no Ø prefix.
rules.fail_condition: Slot width includes a Ø prefix (converting it into a plug weld callout), is omitted, or is placed to the right of the symbol.
rules.remediation: Place the faying-surface slot width to the left of the slot weld symbol without a Ø prefix.

rules.title: Slot Weld Length (Major Axis at Faying Surface) Right of Symbol
rules.audit_check: The length of a slot weld (dimension of the slot in the direction of the major axis at the faying surface) SHALL be shown to the right of the slot weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Slot length at the faying surface appears immediately to the right of the slot weld symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Slot length is missing from the right of the slot weld symbol (making it indistinguishable from a pitch-only callout) or placed to the left of the symbol.
rules.remediation: Place the faying-surface slot length immediately to the right of the slot weld symbol.

rules.title: Included Angle of Countersink Above or Below Slot Weld Symbol
rules.audit_check: The included angle of countersink of slot welds SHALL be located on the same side of the reference line as the weld symbol, directly below (arrow side) or above (other side) the slot weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Included countersink angle is shown directly below an arrow-side slot symbol or above an other-side slot symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Countersink angle is placed inside or beside the slot weld symbol or specified as a single-wall half-angle.
rules.remediation: Place the included countersink angle directly below (arrow side) or above (other side) the slot weld symbol.

rules.title: Partial Depth of Filling Specified Inside Slot Weld Symbol
rules.audit_check: When depth of filling of a slot weld is less than complete, the depth of filling SHALL be specified in inches or millimeters inside the slot weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Partial-fill slot weld shows the numeric depth of filling cleanly inside the rectangular slot weld symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Partial fill depth is placed outside the slot weld symbol or left only as an ambiguous text note.
rules.remediation: Place the partial fill depth inside the rectangular slot weld symbol.

rules.title: Omission of Depth of Filling Defaults to Complete Filling of Slot
rules.audit_check: Omission of a depth-of-filling dimension inside the slot weld symbol specifies complete filling of the slot.
rules.pass_condition: Complete slot filling is intended whenever the slot weld symbol interior is left blank, consistent with all section views and notes.
rules.fail_condition: Slot weld symbol interior is blank while a section view or design requirement indicates partial filling.
rules.remediation: Verify complete filling is intended; if partial filling is required, specify the depth inside the slot weld symbol.

rules.title: Slot Weld Straight-Line Pitch Right of Length After Hyphen (L-P)
rules.audit_check: The pitch (center-to-center spacing) of slot welds in a straight line SHALL be shown to the right of the length dimension and separated from it by a hyphen (L-P).
rules.pass_condition: Multiple inline slot welds show length and center-to-center pitch to the right of the slot symbol formatted as L-P (e.g., 2-6 or 50-150).
rules.fail_condition: Pitch is separated from length by a slash, comma, or '@' symbol, placed before length, or represents clear space instead of center-to-center distance.
rules.remediation: Format inline slot weld length and center-to-center pitch to the right of the symbol as L-P separated by a hyphen.

rules.title: Number of Slot Welds Specified in Parentheses
rules.audit_check: When a definite number of slot welds is desired in a joint, the number SHALL be shown in parentheses on the same side of the reference line as the weld symbol (above/below the symbol, or outside the countersink angle when specified).
rules.pass_condition: Slot weld count is enclosed in parentheses (N) on the same side of the reference line as the slot weld symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Slot weld count omits parentheses, is placed on the opposite side, or is stated inconsistently in notes.
rules.remediation: Show the definite number of slot welds in parentheses (N) on the same side of the reference line above/below the slot symbol.

rules.title: Mandatory Drawing Specification of Slot Weld Location and Orientation
rules.audit_check: The exact location and orientation (major-axis direction and end geometry) of slot welds SHALL be specified directly on the drawing because the welding symbol alone does not convey slot orientation.
rules.pass_condition: Drawing views clearly show and dimension the position and orientation of every slot (or series of slots) referenced by a slot weld symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Slot weld symbol gives width, length, and pitch without drawing views or dimensions establishing slot position and major-axis orientation.
rules.remediation: Add explicit location and orientation dimensions (and slot outline/centerlines) on the drawing view for all slot welds.

rules.title: As-Welded Flush or Convex Contour on Slot Welds
rules.audit_check: Slot welds to be welded approximately flush or convex without mechanical postweld finishing SHALL be specified by adding the flush or convex contour symbol without a finishing letter.
rules.pass_condition: As-welded flush or convex slot weld includes the contour symbol alone with no finishing letter.
rules.fail_condition: As-welded slot contour is called out via non-standard text or erroneously paired with a finishing letter.
rules.remediation: Add only the flush or convex contour symbol to the slot weld symbol when as-welded contour is intended.

rules.title: Postweld-Finished Slot Weld Contour and Flat-Not-Flush Tail Note
visual_syntax_triggers: C G H M P R U
rules.audit_check: Slot welds to be finished flush or convex by mechanical means SHALL specify both the contour symbol and finishing designator (C, G, H, M, P, R, or U); flat-but-not-flush surfaces SHALL be clarified by an explanatory note in the tail.
rules.pass_condition: Postweld-finished slot weld pairs a flush/convex contour symbol with a valid finishing letter, and any flat-not-flush requirement is noted in the tail.
rules.fail_condition: Finishing letter appears without a contour symbol, uses a non-standard code, or omits a tail note for flat-not-flush finishing.
rules.remediation: Combine the contour symbol with the applicable finishing letter (C, G, H, M, P, R, or U) and include a tail note for flat-but-not-flush requirements.

rules.title: Arrow-Side Spot Weld Symbol Placement
rules.audit_check: Spot welds to be made from the arrow side (e.g., arc spot welds such as GTAW or GMAW spot welds where side significance applies) SHALL be indicated by placing the circular spot weld symbol below the reference line.
rules.pass_condition: Arrow-side spot weld places the circular spot weld symbol below and touching the reference line.
rules.fail_condition: A one-sided arc/laser/EB spot weld applied from the arrow side is centered on or placed above the reference line.
rules.remediation: Place the spot weld symbol below the reference line when welding must be executed from the arrow side.

rules.title: Other-Side Spot Weld Symbol Placement
rules.audit_check: Spot welds to be made from the other side SHALL be indicated by placing the circular spot weld symbol above the reference line.
rules.pass_condition: Other-side spot weld places the circular spot weld symbol above and touching the reference line.
rules.fail_condition: Spot weld required from the other side is placed below or centered on the reference line.
rules.remediation: Place the spot weld symbol above the reference line when the weld must be made from the other side.

rules.title: Centered Spot Weld Symbol When No Arrow-Side/Other-Side Significance Exists
rules.audit_check: Spot welds with no arrow-side or other-side significance (such as resistance spot welds, RSW, or ultrasonic spot welds) SHALL be indicated by centering the circular spot weld symbol directly on the reference line.
rules.pass_condition: RSW or other non-sided spot welds center the circle symmetrically across the horizontal reference line.
rules.fail_condition: RSW spot weld with no side significance is arbitrarily placed on one side without justification, or a sided process (e.g., PW) is erroneously centered.
rules.remediation: Center the spot weld symbol on the reference line when the welding process has no arrow-side/other-side significance.

rules.title: Spot Weld Dimensions Placed Consistently on Symbol Side or Either Side When Centered
rules.audit_check: Dimensions of arrow-side or other-side spot welds SHALL be shown on the same side of the reference line as the weld symbol; when the spot weld symbol is centered on the reference line, ALL dimensions SHALL be shown on either the arrow side or the other side (not split inconsistently across both sides).
rules.pass_condition: Sided spot welds place all dimensions on the symbol side; centered spot welds consolidate all dimensions on one chosen side of the reference line.
rules.fail_condition: Dimensions for a sided spot weld appear on the opposite side, or dimensions for a centered spot weld are scattered arbitrarily above and below the reference line.
rules.remediation: Place all spot weld dimensions on the same side as the symbol, or group all dimensions consistently on one side when the symbol is centered.

rules.title: Mandatory Welding Process Reference in Tail for Spot Welds
rules.audit_check: The welding process reference (e.g., RSW, GMAW, GTAW, LBW, EBW, PW) SHALL be indicated in the tail of every spot weld symbol (unless unequivocally established by a general drawing note or referenced specification).
rules.pass_condition: Tail of the spot weld symbol contains a valid AWS Table A.2–A.4 process code (or specification designating the process).
rules.fail_condition: Spot weld symbol omits the tail and process designation with no drawing-wide process specification.
rules.remediation: Add a tail to the spot weld symbol containing the official AWS process designation (e.g., RSW, GTAW, GMAW, PW).

rules.title: Projection Weld Requires 'PW' in Tail and Above/Below (Never Centered) Symbol
rules.audit_check: When projection welding is specified, the projection welding process reference ('PW') SHALL be placed in the tail AND the spot weld symbol SHALL be placed either below (arrow side) or above (other side) the reference line—NEVER centered on the reference line—to identify which member receives the embossed projection.
rules.pass_condition: Projection weld callout has 'PW' in the tail and places the circular symbol strictly below (embossment on arrow-side member) or above (embossment on other-side member) the reference line.
rules.fail_condition: Projection weld symbol is centered on the reference line, omits 'PW' in the tail, or fails to distinguish which member is embossed.
rules.remediation: Include 'PW' in the tail and move the circular symbol either below (arrow-side embossment) or above (other-side embossment) the reference line.

rules.title: Spot Weld Size (Faying-Surface Diameter) Placed Left of Symbol
rules.audit_check: When spot welds are dimensioned by size, the size (diameter of the weld at the faying surface, in inches or millimeters) SHALL be placed to the left of the spot weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Spot weld faying-surface diameter is shown to the left of the circular spot weld symbol in drawing units.
rules.fail_condition: Spot weld size is placed to the right of the symbol, specifies electrode tip diameter instead of weld nugget diameter at the faying surface, or omits units when ambiguous.
rules.remediation: Specify the required weld diameter at the faying surface to the left of the spot weld symbol.

rules.title: Spot Weld Minimum Shear Strength Placed Left of Symbol
rules.audit_check: When spot welds are specified by strength rather than diameter, the minimum acceptable shear strength per spot (in pounds [lb] or newtons [N]) SHALL be placed to the left of the spot weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Minimum shear strength per spot weld (with force units or drawing convention, e.g., 600 lb or 2700 N) appears immediately to the left of the spot weld symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Shear strength value is placed in the tail without clear syntax, placed to the right of the symbol, or conflicts with a simultaneously specified diameter without precedence.
rules.remediation: Place the minimum shear strength per spot weld (in lb or N) to the left of the spot weld symbol.

rules.title: Straight-Line Spot Weld Pitch Placed Right of Symbol
rules.audit_check: The pitch (center-to-center spacing) of spot welds in a straight line SHALL be shown to the right of the spot weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Center-to-center spacing of inline spot welds appears immediately to the right of the circular spot weld symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Pitch is placed to the left of the symbol, omitted for a series of welds lacking drawing dimensions, or given as edge-to-edge gap.
rules.remediation: Place the straight-line center-to-center pitch to the right of the spot weld symbol.

rules.title: Definite Number of Spot Welds Placed in Parentheses
rules.audit_check: When a definite number of spot welds is desired in a joint, the number SHALL be shown in parentheses on the same side of the reference line as the symbol (or above or below when centered on the reference line).
rules.pass_condition: Exact spot weld count is enclosed in parentheses (N) directly above or below the circular spot weld symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Number of spot welds lacks parentheses, is written as '5 PLACES' inconsistently, or conflicts with the pitch and joint length.
rules.remediation: Specify the definite number of spot welds in parentheses (N) directly above or below the spot weld symbol.

rules.title: Grouped Spot Welds Require Arrow to Intersecting Centerline or Clearly Defined Random Area
rules.audit_check: For a group of spot welds located by intersecting centerlines, the arrow SHALL point to at least one of the centerlines passing through each weld location; when spot welds are randomly located in a group, the bounded area in which they are to be applied SHALL be clearly indicated on the drawing.
rules.pass_condition: Grid/pattern spot welds use intersecting centerlines contacted by the arrow(s), and any random spot group clearly outlines and dimensions the permitted weld zone.
rules.fail_condition: A spot weld symbol with count (N) points vaguely to a sheet metal panel without centerlines or a demarcated zone defining where welds belong.
rules.remediation: Draw intersecting centerlines touched by the arrow(s) for patterned spot welds, or clearly bound and dimension the target zone for random spot weld groups.

rules.title: Partial Extent of Spot Welding Must Be Dimensioned on Drawing
rules.audit_check: When spot welding extends less than the full distance between abrupt changes in the direction of the weld, the desired extent SHALL be dimensioned directly on the drawing.
rules.pass_condition: Partial-extent rows of spot welds have explicit start/end or span dimensions shown on the drawing.
rules.fail_condition: Spot welding covers only a partial flange or overlap segment without dimension lines defining where the row starts and terminates.
rules.remediation: Add dimension lines on the drawing defining the exact start, end, and span of partial-extent spot welding.

rules.title: As-Welded Flush or Convex Contour on Spot Welds
rules.audit_check: When the exposed surface of one member of a spot-welded joint is to be welded approximately flush or convex without mechanical finishing, the flush or convex contour symbol SHALL be added to the appropriate side of the spot weld symbol without a finishing designator.
rules.pass_condition: As-welded flush/convex contour symbol appears on the side corresponding to the target exposed member with no finishing letter.
rules.fail_condition: Exposed-surface flush requirement is placed on the wrong side of a centered symbol or lacks the standard contour glyph.
rules.remediation: Place the flush or convex contour symbol (without a finishing letter) on the side of the spot weld symbol corresponding to the exposed member.

rules.title: Postweld-Finished Spot Weld Contour and Flat-Not-Flush Note
visual_syntax_triggers: C G H M P R U
rules.audit_check: Spot welds to be finished flush or convex by mechanical means SHALL specify both the contour symbol and a standard finishing letter (C, G, H, M, P, R, or U); flat-but-not-flush surfaces SHALL include an explanatory note in the tail.
rules.pass_condition: Postweld-finished spot weld displays both contour symbol and valid finishing letter, plus a tail note if flat-not-flush is intended.
rules.fail_condition: Finishing letter appears without contour symbol, uses a non-standard code, or omits tail explanation for flat-not-flush surfaces.
rules.remediation: Combine the contour symbol with the required finishing letter (C, G, H, M, P, R, or U) and add a tail note when flat-not-flush is required.

rules.title: Spot Weld Symbol Applied to Two Outer Members for Multiple-Member Joints
rules.audit_check: For multiple-member spot-welded joints (three or more stacked members fused together), the spot weld symbol SHALL be used for the joint with the arrow indicating the stack/outer members as shown in AWS A2.4 Figure 34.
rules.pass_condition: Multi-sheet spot-weld joint clearly shows all stacked members in the view/section with the spot weld symbol applied unambiguously across the outer members.
rules.fail_condition: Three-or-more-member stack uses conflicting stacked weld symbols or fails to make clear which members are joined in a single spot weld operation.
rules.remediation: Apply the spot weld symbol clearly to the outer members of the multi-member stack (with section view if ply participation is non-obvious).

rules.title: Arrow-Side Seam Weld Symbol Placement
rules.audit_check: Seam welds to be made from the arrow side (e.g., arc, laser, or electron beam seam welds with side significance) SHALL be indicated by placing the seam weld symbol (circle crossed by two parallel horizontal lines) below the reference line.
rules.pass_condition: Arrow-side seam weld displays the seam weld symbol below and touching the reference line.
rules.fail_condition: Arrow-side seam weld symbol is placed above or centered on the reference line.
rules.remediation: Place the seam weld symbol below the reference line when welding is required from the arrow side.

rules.title: Other-Side Seam Weld Symbol Placement
rules.audit_check: Seam welds to be made from the other side SHALL be indicated by placing the seam weld symbol above the reference line.
rules.pass_condition: Other-side seam weld displays the seam weld symbol above and touching the reference line.
rules.fail_condition: Other-side seam weld symbol is placed below or centered on the reference line.
rules.remediation: Place the seam weld symbol above the reference line when welding is required from the other side.

rules.title: Centered Seam Weld Symbol When No Side Significance Exists
rules.audit_check: Seam welds with no arrow-side or other-side significance (such as resistance seam welds, RSEW) SHALL be indicated by centering the seam weld symbol on the reference line.
rules.pass_condition: RSEW or other non-sided seam weld centers the seam weld symbol symmetrically across the horizontal reference line.
rules.fail_condition: RSEW seam weld with no side significance is offset to one side without justification.
rules.remediation: Center the seam weld symbol on the reference line when the seam welding process has no side significance.

rules.title: Seam Weld Dimensions on Symbol Side or Consolidated on One Side When Centered
rules.audit_check: Dimensions of arrow-side or other-side seam welds SHALL be shown on the same side of the reference line as the seam weld symbol; when centered on the reference line, ALL dimensions SHALL be shown on either the arrow side or the other side.
rules.pass_condition: All seam weld dimensions (size/strength, length, pitch, count) are placed on the symbol side, or consolidated on one chosen side when the symbol is centered.
rules.fail_condition: Seam weld dimensions appear on the opposite side of a sided symbol or are split across both sides of a centered symbol.
rules.remediation: Place all seam weld dimensions on the same side as the symbol (or all on one side when centered).

rules.title: Mandatory Welding Process Reference in Tail for Seam Welds
rules.audit_check: The welding process reference (e.g., RSEW, EBW, LBW, GMAW, GTAW) SHALL be indicated in the tail of every seam weld symbol (unless unambiguously controlled by a general note or specification).
rules.pass_condition: Seam weld symbol tail contains a valid AWS Table A.2–A.4 process code.
rules.fail_condition: Seam weld symbol omits the welding process reference in the tail with no controlling general specification.
rules.remediation: Add a tail to the seam weld symbol specifying the official AWS process designation (e.g., RSEW, LBW, EBW, GTAW).

rules.title: Seam Weld Size (Faying-Surface Width) Placed Left of Symbol
rules.audit_check: When seam welds are dimensioned by size, the size (width of the weld at the faying surface, in inches or millimeters) SHALL be placed to the left of the seam weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Faying-surface seam width is shown immediately to the left of the seam weld symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Seam width is placed to the right of the symbol or uses wheel face width rather than faying-surface weld width.
rules.remediation: Specify the seam weld width at the faying surface to the left of the seam weld symbol.

rules.title: Seam Weld Minimum Shear Strength per Linear Unit Placed Left of Symbol
rules.audit_check: When seam welds are specified by strength, the minimum acceptable shear strength (in pounds per linear inch [lb/in] or newtons per millimeter [N/mm]) SHALL be placed to the left of the seam weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Minimum shear strength per unit length (lb/in or N/mm) appears immediately to the left of the seam weld symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Strength is expressed as total joint load rather than force per unit length, lacks units when ambiguous, or is placed to the right of the symbol.
rules.remediation: Specify minimum seam shear strength in lb/in or N/mm to the left of the seam weld symbol.

rules.title: Seam Weld Length Placed Right of Symbol
rules.audit_check: When a specific length of a seam weld is specified, the length dimension SHALL be shown to the right of the seam weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Seam weld length appears immediately to the right of the seam weld symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Seam weld length is placed to the left of the symbol or inside the tail instead of to the right of the symbol.
rules.remediation: Place the seam weld length immediately to the right of the seam weld symbol.

rules.title: Omission of Seam Weld Length Defaults to Full Distance Between Abrupt Direction Changes
rules.audit_check: When a seam weld extends the full distance between abrupt changes in the direction of welding, no length dimension need be shown on the welding symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Omission of a length dimension aligns with full-length continuous seam welding between abrupt corners/edges.
rules.fail_condition: Length is omitted on a seam weld that is meant to stop short of a flange end or corner without any drawing extent dimensions.
rules.remediation: Confirm full-length welding is intended; if partial seam welding is required, specify length on the symbol and/or dimension lines on the drawing.

rules.title: Partial Extent of Seam Welding Must Be Dimensioned on Drawing
rules.audit_check: When a seam weld extends less than the full distance between abrupt changes in direction, the exact location and extent SHALL be dimensioned on the drawing.
rules.pass_condition: Partial seam weld segments have explicit location and extent dimensions on the drawing.
rules.fail_condition: A seam weld specifies a shorter length than the joint without drawing dimensions defining where the seam starts and stops.
rules.remediation: Add dimension lines on the drawing locating the start and termination of the partial seam weld.

rules.title: Intermittent Seam Weld Pitch Defined as Center-to-Center Distance
rules.audit_check: The pitch of intermittent seam welds SHALL be the center-to-center distance between adjacent weld increments (therefore pitch MUST always be greater than segment length L).
rules.pass_condition: Intermittent seam pitch represents center-to-center spacing and satisfies P > L.
rules.fail_condition: Pitch is less than or equal to segment length (P <= L) or specifies clear gap between weld ends instead of center-to-center pitch.
rules.remediation: Convert spacing to center-to-center pitch so P > L and update the symbol accordingly.

rules.title: Intermittent Seam Weld Pitch Placed Right of Length Following Hyphen (L-P)
rules.audit_check: The pitch of intermittent seam welds SHALL be shown to the right of the length dimension and separated from it by a hyphen (L-P).
rules.pass_condition: Intermittent seam weld shows length and pitch to the right of the seam symbol formatted as L-P (e.g., 2-4 or 50-100).
rules.fail_condition: Length and pitch are separated by a non-standard character (e.g., '/' or '@') or placed in reversed order.
rules.remediation: Format intermittent seam weld length and pitch as L-P immediately to the right of the seam weld symbol.

rules.title: Definite Number of Seam Welds Placed in Parentheses
rules.audit_check: When a definite number of seam welds is desired in a joint, the number SHALL be shown in parentheses on the same side of the reference line as the symbol (or above or below when centered).
rules.pass_condition: Definite seam weld count appears in parentheses (N) above or below the seam weld symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Seam weld count omits parentheses or is placed in an ambiguous location.
rules.remediation: Place the definite number of seam welds in parentheses (N) above or below the seam weld symbol.

rules.title: Default Orientation of Intermittent Seam Welds Parallel to Weld Axis
rules.audit_check: Unless otherwise indicated, intermittent seam welds SHALL be understood to have their length and pitch measured parallel to the axis of the weld.
rules.pass_condition: Intermittent seam segments run longitudinally along the joint axis when no detail view specifies transverse/angled orientation.
rules.fail_condition: Transverse or oblique intermittent seam welds are intended but rely on a standard L-P symbol without a detail view.
rules.remediation: Confirm longitudinal orientation along the weld axis, or add a detailed view per Clause 11.6.2 if non-parallel orientation is required.

rules.title: Non-Parallel Intermittent Seam Weld Orientation Requires Detailed Drawing
rules.audit_check: When intermittent seam welds are oriented other than parallel to the weld axis (e.g., transverse or angled segments), the orientation SHALL be clarified by a detailed drawing.
rules.pass_condition: Non-parallel intermittent seam welds include a detail view explicitly showing weld segment angle, length, and pitch direction.
rules.fail_condition: Non-parallel or transverse intermittent seam welds are specified only by a symbol without a clarifying detail view.
rules.remediation: Provide a detail view showing the exact orientation, segment direction, and pitch geometry of non-parallel intermittent seam welds.

rules.title: As-Welded Flush or Convex Contour on Seam Welds
rules.audit_check: When the exposed surface of one member of a seam-welded joint is to be welded approximately flush or convex without mechanical finishing, the flush or convex contour symbol SHALL be added on the corresponding side without a finishing letter.
rules.pass_condition: As-welded flush/convex contour symbol is placed on the target member's side of the seam weld symbol without a finishing letter.
rules.fail_condition: Contour symbol is missing, placed on the wrong side, or paired with an unintended finishing letter.
rules.remediation: Add the flush or convex contour symbol (without a finishing letter) on the side of the seam weld symbol corresponding to the exposed member.

rules.title: Postweld-Finished Seam Weld Contour and Flat-Not-Flush Note
visual_syntax_triggers: C G H M P R U
rules.audit_check: Seam welds to be finished flush or convex by mechanical means SHALL show both the contour symbol and a valid finishing letter (C, G, H, M, P, R, or U); flat-but-not-flush surfaces SHALL include an explanatory note in the tail.
rules.pass_condition: Mechanically finished seam weld pairs contour symbol + valid finishing letter, with a tail note whenever flat-not-flush is intended.
rules.fail_condition: Finishing letter appears without a contour symbol, uses a non-standard code, or lacks a tail explanation for flat-not-flush finishing.
rules.remediation: Pair the flush or convex contour symbol with the required finishing letter (C, G, H, M, P, R, or U) and add a tail note for flat-not-flush surfaces.

rules.title: Seam Weld Symbol Applied to Two Outer Members for Multiple-Member Joints
rules.audit_check: For multiple-member seam-welded joints (three or more stacked members), the seam weld symbol SHALL be used for the two outer members as illustrated in AWS A2.4 Figure 39.
rules.pass_condition: Multi-member seam weld applies the seam weld symbol cleanly to the outer members with the full stack clearly depicted.
rules.fail_condition: Multiple-member seam weld uses ambiguous or stacked symbols that obscure which plies are welded.
rules.remediation: Apply the seam weld symbol to the outer members of the stack and show all plies clearly in the view or section.

rules.title: Edge Weld Symbol Scope, Full-Thickness Fusion Requirement, and Drawing Flange Dimensions
rules.audit_check: The edge weld symbol SHALL be used only on edge joints, flanged butt joints, and flanged corner joints where the full thickness of the joint members is fused; all flange heights, bend radii, and member thicknesses SHALL be dimensioned on the drawing, never inside the welding symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Edge weld symbol is applied to an edge, flanged butt, or flanged corner joint with full member-edge thickness fusion intended, and flange geometry is dimensioned directly on the drawing.
rules.fail_condition: Edge weld symbol is used on a butt/lap/T-joint without flanged edges, used where only partial member thickness is fused (should be groove or surfacing), or flange height/radius dimensions are stuffed into the welding symbol.
rules.remediation: Restrict edge weld symbols to edge, flanged butt, and flanged corner joints requiring full-thickness fusion, and dimension all flange geometry on the drawing.

rules.title: Edge Weld Size Placed Left of Symbol on Same Side
rules.audit_check: When an edge weld size (weld thickness from the weld face to the root) is specified, it SHALL be placed to the left of the edge weld symbol on the same side of the reference line (size may be omitted when not required).
rules.pass_condition: Specified edge weld size appears immediately to the left of the edge weld symbol on the same side of the reference line.
rules.fail_condition: Edge weld size is placed to the right of the symbol, on the opposite side of the reference line, or written ambiguously in a note.
rules.remediation: Place the specified edge weld size immediately to the left of the edge weld symbol on the same side of the reference line.

rules.title: Double-Edge Weld Symbol Restricted to Edge Joints Only (Forbidden on Flanged Joints)
rules.audit_check: Double-edge weld symbols (edge weld symbols on both sides of the reference line) SHALL be used ONLY on edge joints—NEVER on flanged butt or flanged corner joints; welding both sides of flanged butt or flanged corner joints SHALL combine an edge weld symbol on the edge side with a flare-V-groove or flare-bevel-groove weld symbol on the opposite side.
rules.pass_condition: Double-edge weld symbols appear only on true edge joints; two-sided flanged butt/corner joints pair an edge weld symbol with a flare-V or flare-bevel groove symbol on the opposite side.
rules.fail_condition: A double-edge weld symbol is applied to a flanged butt joint or flanged corner joint where the opposite side forms a curved flare groove rather than two parallel edges.
rules.remediation: Replace the opposite-side edge weld symbol on flanged butt or flanged corner joints with a flare-V-groove or flare-bevel-groove weld symbol.

rules.title: Edge Weld with Complete Joint Penetration Uses Opposite-Side Melt-Through Symbol
rules.audit_check: Edge welds requiring complete joint penetration (CJP) on flanged butt or flanged corner joints welded from one side SHALL be specified by placing the melt-through symbol on the side of the reference line opposite the edge weld symbol (edge weld size is unnecessary when melt-through is specified).
rules.pass_condition: Single-side CJP flanged edge weld places the solid semicircular melt-through symbol opposite the edge weld symbol (with optional melt-through height to the left of the melt-through symbol).
rules.fail_condition: Single-side flanged edge weld relies only on a text note for melt-through or places the melt-through symbol on the same side as the edge weld symbol.
rules.remediation: Add the melt-through symbol on the side of the reference line opposite the edge weld symbol to specify CJP on flanged butt or flanged corner joints.

rules.title: Edge Welds on Joints with More Than Two Members
rules.audit_check: Edge welds on joints consisting of more than two members SHOULD use the edge weld symbol in the same manner as two-member edge joints, with all participating members clearly shown on the drawing.
rules.pass_condition: Multi-member edge joint applies a single edge weld symbol cleanly to the aligned edges with all members clearly depicted.
rules.fail_condition: Multi-member edge joint uses duplicated or ambiguous weld symbols that obscure whether all stacked edges are fused together.
rules.remediation: Use a single standard edge weld symbol pointing to the aligned edge joint and clearly depict all participating members.

rules.title: Edge Weld Length Placed Right of Symbol
rules.audit_check: When specified, the length of an edge weld SHALL be shown to the right of the edge weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Edge weld length appears immediately to the right of the edge weld symbol on the same side of the reference line.
rules.fail_condition: Edge weld length is placed to the left of the symbol or on the opposite side of the reference line.
rules.remediation: Place the edge weld length immediately to the right of the edge weld symbol.

rules.title: Omission of Edge Weld Length Defaults to Full Length Between Abrupt Direction Changes
rules.audit_check: When an edge weld extends the full length of the joint between abrupt changes in direction, no length dimension need be shown on the welding symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Omitted length accurately reflects full-length continuous edge welding between abrupt corners/terminations.
rules.fail_condition: Length is omitted on an edge weld intended to be partial-length without drawing extent dimensions.
rules.remediation: Verify full-length welding is intended; otherwise add explicit length and location dimensions.

rules.title: Specific Lengths and Locations of Edge Welds via Dimension Lines
rules.audit_check: Specific lengths and locations of partial edge welds SHOULD be indicated using dimension lines and extension lines directly on the drawing in conjunction with the welding symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Partial-length edge welds are located unambiguously on the drawing using dimension lines.
rules.fail_condition: A partial edge weld specifies length in the symbol (e.g., 50) without indicating where along the edge the segment lies.
rules.remediation: Add dimension lines locating the start and end of each partial edge weld segment.

rules.title: Hatching Permitted to Graphically Indicate Edge Weld Extent
rules.audit_check: Hatching MAY be used to graphically indicate the extent of edge welds on the drawing, provided extent dimensions remain clear and unambiguous.
rules.pass_condition: When hatching is used to depict edge weld extent, its boundaries align cleanly with dimension lines and the welding symbol arrow.
rules.fail_condition: Hatching conflicts with specified weld lengths or is left undimensioned where exact start/stop tolerances matter.
rules.remediation: Ensure any edge weld extent hatching matches the dimensioned weld lengths and arrow callout.

rules.title: Edge Weld Extent Stops at Abrupt Direction Changes per Clause 5.9.2
rules.audit_check: Edge welds SHALL follow Clause 5.9.2 at abrupt changes in joint direction: a single arrow applies only between abrupt direction changes unless multiple arrows or the weld-all-around symbol are properly applied.
rules.pass_condition: Edge welds around corners or closed perimeters use multiple arrows or the weld-all-around symbol (only where geometry remains a valid edge weld all around).
rules.fail_condition: A single-arrow edge weld symbol without weld-all-around is expected to wrap around abrupt 90° corners.
rules.remediation: Use multiple arrows pointing to each edge segment, or add the weld-all-around symbol if the continuous perimeter is uniformly an edge weld.

rules.title: Intermittent Edge Weld Pitch Defined as Center-to-Center Distance
rules.audit_check: The pitch of intermittent edge welds SHALL be the center-to-center distance between adjacent weld increments on one side of the joint (P > L).
rules.pass_condition: Pitch of intermittent edge welds represents center-to-center spacing and exceeds segment length (P > L).
rules.fail_condition: Pitch is less than or equal to segment length (P <= L) or specifies clear unwelded gap instead of center-to-center distance.
rules.remediation: Specify intermittent edge weld pitch as center-to-center distance with P > L.

rules.title: Intermittent Edge Weld Pitch Placed Right of Length Following Hyphen (L-P)
rules.audit_check: The pitch of intermittent edge welds SHALL be shown to the right of the length dimension and separated from it by a hyphen (L-P).
rules.pass_condition: Intermittent edge weld displays L-P to the right of the edge weld symbol with a hyphen separator.
rules.fail_condition: Length and pitch use an invalid separator or reversed order.
rules.remediation: Format intermittent edge weld length and pitch as L-P immediately to the right of the edge weld symbol.

rules.title: Chain Intermittent Edge Welds Dimensioned on Both Sides with Aligned Symbols
rules.audit_check: Chain intermittent edge welds (applicable to true edge joints) SHALL have their dimensions shown on BOTH sides of the reference line with the arrow-side and other-side edge weld symbols directly opposite (aligned with) each other.
rules.pass_condition: Chain intermittent double-edge weld aligns both edge symbols vertically opposite each other and shows L-P on both sides.
rules.fail_condition: Dimensions are shown on only one side of a chain intermittent double-edge symbol, or symbols are staggered when chain alignment is intended.
rules.remediation: Align arrow-side and other-side edge weld symbols directly opposite each other and specify dimensions on both sides.

rules.title: Staggered Intermittent Edge Welds Dimensioned on Both Sides with Offset Symbols
rules.audit_check: Staggered intermittent edge welds SHALL have their dimensions shown on BOTH sides of the reference line with the arrow-side and other-side edge weld symbols horizontally offset (staggered) relative to each other.
rules.pass_condition: Staggered intermittent double-edge weld offsets the upper and lower edge weld symbols horizontally and displays dimensions on both sides.
rules.fail_condition: Edge weld symbols are vertically aligned despite a note requesting staggered welds, or dimensions appear on only one side.
rules.remediation: Offset the arrow-side and other-side edge weld symbols horizontally and include dimensions on both sides of the reference line.

rules.title: Intermittent Edge Weld End Segments and Unwelded End Spacing Rule
rules.audit_check: When intermittent edge welds are combined with continuous end welds or special end segments, separate welding symbols and dimension lines SHALL specify the end segments; unless otherwise specified, intermittent edge welds begin and end with full increments and any unwelded space at the ends SHOULD NOT exceed the clear spacing between increments.
rules.pass_condition: Special end segments use separate welding symbols and extent dimensions, and standard intermittent runs fit cleanly without excessive unwelded end overhangs.
rules.fail_condition: Continuous end welds are combined with intermittent runs under a single ambiguous symbol, or end geometry leaves unwelded ends wider than the clear space between increments without explicit dimensioning.
rules.remediation: Use separate welding symbols and extent dimensions for end segments or non-standard end offsets.

rules.title: Non-Obvious Intermittent Edge Weld Locations Require Dimension Lines or Hatching
rules.audit_check: Where the exact location of intermittent edge welds is not obvious (e.g., interrupted by cutouts, notches, or non-uniform spans), the locations SHALL be indicated by dimension lines or hatching on the drawing.
rules.pass_condition: Interrupted or non-obvious intermittent edge weld runs are explicitly located using dimension lines or hatching.
rules.fail_condition: An intermittent edge weld symbol is applied to a notched or interrupted edge without showing where segments start, stop, or skip cutouts.
rules.remediation: Add dimension lines or hatching on the drawing to clearly locate intermittent edge weld segments around features and boundaries.

rules.title: Stud Weld Symbol Has Arrow-Side Significance Only (Must Be Below Reference Line)
rules.audit_check: The stud weld symbol (circle enclosing an X) does NOT indicate a joint and has arrow-side significance ONLY: it SHALL always be placed BELOW the reference line (NEVER above or on both sides), and the arrow SHALL point clearly to the surface to which the stud is to be welded.
rules.pass_condition: Stud weld symbol is placed strictly below the reference line and the arrow terminates clearly on the target mounting surface.
rules.fail_condition: Stud weld symbol is placed above the reference line, on both sides, or centered on the reference line, or the arrow points ambiguously to an edge rather than the mounting face.
rules.remediation: Move the stud weld symbol below the reference line and point the arrow unambiguously to the surface receiving the stud(s).

rules.title: Stud Weld Size (Stud Diameter) Placed Left of Symbol
rules.audit_check: The size (nominal diameter of the stud) SHALL be placed to the left of the stud weld symbol (stud length, thread spec, or material belongs in the tail or parts list/drawing).
rules.pass_condition: Stud nominal diameter appears immediately to the left of the stud weld symbol below the reference line.
rules.fail_condition: Stud size is placed to the right of the symbol, omitted without a controlling parts-list/tail reference, or confused with pitch.
rules.remediation: Place the stud nominal diameter immediately to the left of the stud weld symbol.

rules.title: Straight-Line Stud Pitch Right of Symbol vs. Non-Linear Spacing on Drawing
rules.audit_check: The pitch (center-to-center spacing) of stud welds in a straight line SHALL be shown to the right of the stud weld symbol; spacing of stud welds not in a straight line SHALL be dimensioned directly on the drawing.
rules.pass_condition: Straight-line stud center-to-center pitch is placed immediately to the right of the stud weld symbol, while circular, staggered, or matrix stud patterns are fully dimensioned on the drawing.
rules.fail_condition: Straight-line stud pitch is placed on the wrong side of the symbol, or non-linear stud patterns rely on a single symbol pitch without drawing coordinates.
rules.remediation: Place straight-line center-to-center pitch to the right of the stud weld symbol and dimension any non-linear stud pattern on the drawing.

rules.title: Number of Stud Welds Placed in Parentheses Below Symbol
rules.audit_check: The number of stud welds in a line or group SHALL be shown in parentheses directly below the stud weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Stud weld quantity appears enclosed in parentheses (N) directly beneath the stud weld symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Stud quantity omits parentheses, is placed above the reference line, or is placed to the left/right of the symbol.
rules.remediation: Place the stud count in parentheses (N) directly below the stud weld symbol.

rules.title: All Stud Weld Dimensions Must Remain on Arrow Side of Reference Line
rules.audit_check: All dimensions of stud welds (size, pitch, and count) SHALL be placed on the same (arrow) side of the reference line as the stud weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Size, pitch, and (N) count all reside below the reference line alongside the stud weld symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Any stud weld dimension is placed above the reference line.
rules.remediation: Relocate all stud weld dimensions below the reference line on the same side as the stud weld symbol.

rules.title: Location of First and Last Stud in Each Single Line Must Be Specified on Drawing
rules.audit_check: The location of the first and last stud weld in each single line SHALL be specified directly on the drawing using dimension lines.
rules.pass_condition: Every line of stud welds has explicit drawing dimensions locating both the first stud and the last stud (plus centerline offset).
rules.fail_condition: A row of studs specifies pitch and count in the welding symbol without drawing dimensions locating the start and end studs.
rules.remediation: Dimension the exact positions of the first and last stud welds in every stud line on the drawing.

rules.title: Surfacing Built Up by Single or Multiple Passes Requires Surfacing Weld Symbol
rules.audit_check: Surfaces to be built up by welding (cladding, hardfacing, buttering, or dimensional buildup), whether by single-pass or multiple-pass parallel/overlapping beads, SHALL be indicated by the surfacing weld symbol (two adjacent semicircular loops).
rules.pass_condition: Weld overlay, cladding, hardfacing, or buttering surfaces are specified using the standard surfacing weld symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Weld buildup or cladding is called out using an improper fillet/groove symbol or an invented cross-hatch note without a surfacing weld symbol.
rules.remediation: Use the AWS A2.4 surfacing weld symbol to specify single- or multiple-pass weld buildup, cladding, hardfacing, or buttering.

rules.title: Surfacing Weld Symbol Has Arrow-Side Significance Only (Must Be Below Reference Line)
rules.audit_check: The surfacing weld symbol does NOT indicate the welding of a joint and has arrow-side significance ONLY: it SHALL always be placed BELOW the reference line (NEVER above or on both sides), with the arrow pointing clearly to the surface to be built up.
rules.pass_condition: Surfacing weld symbol sits strictly below the reference line and the arrow points directly to the surface receiving weld buildup.
rules.fail_condition: Surfacing weld symbol is placed above the reference line, on both sides, or centered on the reference line.
rules.remediation: Move the surfacing weld symbol below the reference line and point the arrow unambiguously to the target surface (use separate symbols if opposite faces both require surfacing).

rules.title: Surfacing Weld Dimensions Must Remain on Arrow Side of Reference Line
rules.audit_check: Dimensions used in conjunction with the surfacing weld symbol SHALL be placed on the same (arrow) side of the reference line as the weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Minimum buildup thickness and any contour/finishing symbols appear below the reference line with the surfacing weld symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Surfacing thickness or contour symbols are placed above the reference line.
rules.remediation: Move all surfacing weld dimensions and supplementary symbols below the reference line.

rules.title: Minimum Surfacing Thickness Placed Left of Symbol and Direction in Tail or Drawing
rules.audit_check: The size (minimum thickness) of a surface built up by welding SHALL be indicated by placing the minimum buildup height to the left of the surfacing weld symbol; required bead direction (e.g., axial, circumferential) may be indicated in the tail or on the drawing.
rules.pass_condition: Minimum required surfacing thickness appears immediately to the left of the surfacing weld symbol, and any required bead orientation is clearly stated in the tail or drawing.
rules.fail_condition: Buildup thickness is placed to the right of the surfacing symbol or given as a conflicting final part thickness without clarifying minimum weld deposit height.
rules.remediation: Place the minimum surfacing weld deposit thickness to the left of the surfacing weld symbol and note any required bead direction in the tail or drawing.

rules.title: Multiple Surfacing Layers Specified via Multiple Reference Lines
rules.audit_check: Multiple surfacing layers (e.g., a buttering/buffer layer followed by a hardfacing overlay) SHOULD be specified using multiple reference lines per Clause 5.7, with the required minimum thickness of each layer placed to the left of its respective surfacing weld symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Multi-layer surfacing uses stacked reference lines sequenced from nearest the arrow (1st layer) outward, each showing its thickness to the left and filler/process in the tail.
rules.fail_condition: Dissimilar multi-layer cladding/hardfacing sequences are compressed into a single surfacing symbol with ambiguous layer thicknesses or order.
rules.remediation: Use stacked multiple reference lines (nearest arrow = first layer) with each layer's minimum thickness to the left of its surfacing symbol and filler/process in the tail.

rules.title: Omission of Surfacing Thickness When No Specific Height Is Required
rules.audit_check: When no specific buildup thickness is required (e.g., buildup to restore a final machined profile governed by drawing part dimensions), the size dimension to the left of the surfacing weld symbol may be omitted.
rules.pass_condition: Omission of surfacing thickness occurs only where final finished geometry or a referenced procedure defines adequate buildup without needing a minimum deposit thickness.
rules.fail_condition: Surfacing thickness is omitted on a cladding or hardfacing layer where corrosion/wear resistance requires a minimum deposit thickness.
rules.remediation: Confirm whether minimum deposit thickness is controlled elsewhere; for cladding or hardfacing, specify the minimum thickness to the left of the surfacing symbol.

rules.title: Entire Surface Buildup Requires No Area Dimension Other Than Thickness
rules.audit_check: When the entire area of a plane or curved surface is to be built up by welding, no extent dimension other than deposit thickness (if required) need be shown on the drawing.
rules.pass_condition: Omission of area boundary dimensions accurately means the entire surface pointed to by the arrow is to be surfaced.
rules.fail_condition: Area extent is omitted when only a localized pad or wear strip is intended to be surfaced.
rules.remediation: Verify the entire face is to be surfaced; if only a portion of the surface is to be built up, bound and dimension the partial area per Clause 14.3.2.

rules.title: Partial Area Surfacing Requires Explicit Extent, Location, and Orientation on Drawing
rules.audit_check: When only a portion of the area of a plane or curved surface is to be built up by welding, the extent, location, and orientation of the area to be surfaced SHALL be explicitly indicated and dimensioned on the drawing.
rules.pass_condition: Partial-area cladding/hardfacing zones are clearly outlined and dimensioned with location, span, and orientation on the drawing.
rules.fail_condition: Surfacing symbol points to a partial area of a shaft, plate, or flange without explicit boundary and location dimensions.
rules.remediation: Outline and dimension the exact extent, location, and orientation of the partial surfacing zone directly on the drawing.

rules.title: Surfacing a Previously Welded Joint via Multiple Reference Lines
rules.audit_check: When surfacing is to be deposited over a previously completed weld (e.g., corrosion-resistant overlay over a structural groove weld), multiple reference lines per Clause 5.7 SHOULD be used so the structural weld is nearest the arrow (1st operation) and the surfacing symbol is on the subsequent reference line.
rules.pass_condition: Joint weld appears on the first reference line nearest the arrow and the surfacing weld symbol appears on the second reference line.
rules.fail_condition: Joint welding and subsequent weld overlay are combined on a single reference line or sequenced in reverse order.
rules.remediation: Separate the joint weld (1st reference line, nearest arrow) and the overlay surfacing weld (2nd reference line) using multiple reference lines.

rules.title: Surfacing Used to Adjust Joint Dimensions (e.g., Root Opening Buttering)
rules.audit_check: When surfacing (buttering) is specified to adjust member or joint dimensions prior to joining (such as reducing an excessive root opening or building up a groove face), the surfacing weld symbol SHOULD be accompanied by clear extent/dimension callouts and sequenced before the joining weld.
rules.pass_condition: Dimensional-adjustment surfacing specifies the buttered face, thickness/final dimension, and operation order before final joint welding.
rules.fail_condition: Buttering/dimensional-correction surfacing omits target buildup dimensions or fails to identify which joint face is built up.
rules.remediation: Use a surfacing weld symbol pointing to the specific face with required buildup thickness/final dimensions and clear operation sequencing.

rules.title: Mandatory Adequate Brazing Symbols on Drawings of Brazed Assemblies
rules.audit_check: All drawings of brazed assemblies MUST include adequate AWS A2.4 brazing symbols clearly designating the designer's requirements (brazing process, joint clearance, overlap, filler metal/spec, and any joint preparation).
rules.pass_condition: Every brazed joint on the drawing has a complete AWS A2.4 brazing symbol or clearly referenced brazing specification defining process and joint requirements.
rules.fail_condition: Brazed joints rely only on vague notes such as 'BRAZE' without process code, joint clearance, overlap, or filler specification.
rules.remediation: Provide complete AWS A2.4 brazing symbols specifying the brazing process in the tail along with required clearance, overlap, and filler/procedure references.

rules.title: Fillet Symbol for Braze Fillet Restricted Strictly to Flat Horizontal Position
rules.audit_check: The fillet weld symbol SHALL be used to specify a braze fillet ONLY when the assembly can be brazed in the flat (horizontal) position (generally applicable only to torch brazing, TB); molten brazing filler metal is too fluid to form a controlled fillet in vertical, horizontal-wall, or overhead positions.
rules.pass_condition: Any brazing symbol employing a fillet symbol applies to a flat-position braze joint (typically TB) with filler and size clearly specified.
rules.fail_condition: A fillet symbol is applied to a vertical/overhead brazed joint or a furnace-brazed capillary joint where a controlled structural braze fillet cannot be formed.
rules.remediation: Remove the fillet symbol on non-flat or furnace-brazed joints; specify capillary lap/scarf clearance and overlap per Clauses 15.3–15.4, or confirm flat-position TB orientation.

rules.title: Brazing Joint Without Special Preparation Uses Reference Line, Arrow, and Process in Tail
rules.audit_check: When no special joint preparation other than cleaning is required for a brazed joint, the brazing symbol SHOULD consist of an arrow, a reference line, and a tail containing the official AWS brazing process designation (e.g., TB, FB, IB, DB, RB, DFB, BB, IRB, EXB, AB).
rules.pass_condition: Simple capillary brazed joints use an arrow, reference line, and tail specifying a valid AWS Table A.2 brazing process code.
rules.fail_condition: Brazing symbol uses a non-standard process abbreviation or attaches an unnecessary weld groove glyph when no special edge preparation exists.
rules.remediation: Use an arrow, horizontal reference line, and tail containing the official AWS Table A.2 brazing process code (e.g., TB, FB, IB).

rules.title: Application of Conventional Symbols to Brazed Joints (Clearance CL, Overlap L, Fillet Size S)
rules.audit_check: Conventional weld symbols (e.g., square, scarf, bevel, fillet) applied to brazed joints SHOULD follow AWS A2.4 Figure 49 conventions, clearly indicating joint clearance ('CL'), lap/overlap length, or fillet size in standard locations with the brazing process designated in the tail.
rules.pass_condition: Brazed scarf, butt, or lap joints using conventional weld glyphs place clearance (CL), overlap length, or fillet size cleanly in Figure 49 positions with the brazing process in the tail.
rules.fail_condition: Brazed joint applies a weld symbol without identifying the brazing process in the tail (causing misinterpretation as fusion welding) or places clearance/overlap values ambiguously.
rules.remediation: Add the brazing process code in the tail and format clearance (CL), overlap, and joint preparation per AWS A2.4 Figure 49.

rules.title: Six Standard Elements of a Nondestructive Examination Symbol
rules.audit_check: Nondestructive examination (NDE) symbols SHALL be constructed from the six AWS A2.4 elements: (1) reference line, (2) arrow, (3) examination method letter designation(s), (4) extent and number of examinations, (5) supplementary symbols, and (6) tail (with reference line, arrow, and method letter designation mandatory).
rules.pass_condition: Every NDE symbol contains at minimum a horizontal reference line, an arrow pointing to the examined feature/weld, and a valid method letter designation.
rules.fail_condition: NDE callout uses a floating letter code without a reference line/arrow, or omits the examination method letter designation.
rules.remediation: Construct every NDE symbol using a horizontal reference line, arrow, valid method letter designation, and applicable extent/supplementary/tail elements.

rules.title: NDE Method Letter Designations Must Match Table A.6
