rules.audit_check: Nondestructive examination methods SHALL be designated using the official AWS A2.4 Table A.6 letter codes: AET (Acoustic Emission), ET (Electromagnetic), LT (Leak), MP (Magnetic Particle — note: AWS A2.4:2007 Table A.6 prints 'MP' while Clause 16 text/figures show 'MT'; flag non-standard codes like 'X-RAY', 'MPI', 'LPI', 'DYE PEN', 'MAG PARTICLE'), NRT (Neutron Radiographic), PT (Penetrant), PRT (Proof), RT (Radiographic), UT (Ultrasonic), and VT (Visual).
rules.pass_condition: NDE symbol uses official AWS A2.4 letter designations (AET, ET, LT, MP/MT, NRT, PT, PRT, RT, UT, VT).
rules.fail_condition: Drawing uses informal or non-standard NDE abbreviations such as 'X-RAY', 'MPI', 'LPI', 'FPI', 'DPI', 'EC', 'AE', or 'VISUAL' on the NDE reference line.
rules.remediation: Replace non-standard NDE abbreviations with the official AWS A2.4 Table A.6 letter designations (AET, ET, LT, MP [or MT per Clause 16 figures], NRT, PT, PRT, RT, UT, VT).

rules.title: Standard Supplementary NDE Symbols (Figure 50)
rules.audit_check: Supplementary NDE symbols (examine-all-around circle, field examination flag, and radiation direction symbol) SHALL conform strictly to AWS A2.4 Figure 50.
rules.pass_condition: All supplementary NDE glyphs match the exact Figure 50 forms.
rules.fail_condition: Non-standard shapes or free-text substitutions are used in place of Figure 50 supplementary NDE symbols.
rules.remediation: Replace ad-hoc supplementary markings with standard AWS A2.4 Figure 50 NDE supplementary symbols.

rules.title: Standard Location of NDE Symbol Elements (Figure 51)
rules.audit_check: All NDE symbol elements SHALL be positioned strictly in their AWS A2.4 Figure 51 standard locations: method letter designation on/above/below reference line, length or percentage (L or %) to the right of the letter designation, number of examinations (N) in parentheses away from the reference line above/below the letter designation, examine-all-around/field flag at the arrow-reference junction, and specifications/procedures in the tail.
rules.pass_condition: Every NDE symbol element occupies its exact Figure 51 position.
rules.fail_condition: Length, percentage, or count (N) is placed to the left of the NDE letter designation or inside the tail instead of its Figure 51 location.
rules.remediation: Relocate all NDE symbol elements to their mandatory AWS A2.4 Figure 51 standard positions.

rules.title: NDE Arrow Connects Reference Line to Examined Part Defining Arrow Side vs. Other Side
rules.audit_check: The NDE arrow SHALL connect the reference line to the part or weld to be examined; the side of the part to which the arrow points is the arrow side, and the opposite side is the other side.
rules.pass_condition: NDE arrow cleanly contacts the specific weld or part surface so arrow side and other side are unmistakable.
rules.fail_condition: NDE arrow floats near an assembly or points ambiguously where examined side cannot be identified.
rules.remediation: Terminate the NDE arrow directly on the target weld or surface in a view where arrow side and other side are clear.

rules.title: Arrow-Side NDE Method Placed Below Reference Line
rules.audit_check: Examinations to be made on the arrow side of the part SHALL be indicated by placing the NDE method letter designation BELOW the reference line.
rules.pass_condition: Arrow-side NDE method code (e.g., PT, VT, UT) is located below the reference line.
rules.fail_condition: An arrow-side-only examination is placed above or centered on the reference line.
rules.remediation: Place the NDE method letter designation below the reference line for arrow-side examinations.

rules.title: Other-Side NDE Method Placed Above Reference Line
rules.audit_check: Examinations to be made on the other side of the part SHALL be indicated by placing the NDE method letter designation ABOVE the reference line.
rules.pass_condition: Other-side NDE method code is located above the reference line.
rules.fail_condition: An other-side-only examination is placed below or centered on the reference line.
rules.remediation: Place the NDE method letter designation above the reference line for other-side examinations.

rules.title: Both-Sides NDE Method Placed on Both Sides of Reference Line
rules.audit_check: Examinations to be made on BOTH sides of the part SHALL be indicated by placing the NDE method letter designations on BOTH sides of the reference line.
rules.pass_condition: Both-sides examination (e.g., PT or VT on both weld faces) shows the letter designation both above and below the reference line.
rules.fail_condition: Both-sides inspection is attempted using a single centered code or a text note 'BOTH SIDES' instead of placing codes on both sides of the reference line.
rules.remediation: Place the NDE method letter designation on both sides (above and below) of the reference line.

rules.title: Centered NDE Method When No Arrow-Side/Other-Side Significance or Preference Exists
rules.audit_check: When NDE letter designations have no arrow-side or other-side significance, or there is no preference as to which side the examination is made from, the letter designations SHALL be centered ON (straddling) the reference line (with the reference line broken through the letters).
rules.pass_condition: Non-sided or no-preference NDE codes (e.g., RT, LT, AET, or UT with no side preference) are centered directly on the reference line.
rules.fail_condition: A centered NDE code is used where side-specific surface inspection is required, or non-sided methods are arbitrarily placed on one side creating unintended side restrictions.
rules.remediation: Center the NDE letter designation on the reference line whenever no side significance or side preference applies.

rules.title: Multiple NDE Methods on Same Side or Centered Must Be Separated by '+'
rules.audit_check: When more than one NDE method is specified on the same side of the reference line (or centered on the reference line), the method letter designations SHALL be separated by a plus sign ('+'), e.g., UT+RT, LT+PRT, VT+PT.
rules.pass_condition: Combined NDE codes on the same side or centered on the reference line use '+' as the separator (e.g., UT+RT, VT+MT).
rules.fail_condition: Multiple NDE methods are separated by a comma, slash ('/'), ampersand ('&'), space, or hyphen instead of '+' (e.g., 'UT/RT' or 'VT, PT').
rules.remediation: Separate combined NDE method letter designations on the same side or centered on the reference line with a plus sign ('+').

rules.title: Combination of Welding Symbols and NDE Symbols
rules.audit_check: NDE symbols and welding symbols MAY be combined on a single arrow using multiple reference lines (with the welding symbol on the first reference line nearest the arrow and the NDE symbol on the subsequent reference line) or combined on one reference line only where unambiguous.
rules.pass_condition: Combined welding and NDE symbols maintain crisp sequence and clear separation of weld dimensions from NDE extent/percentage callouts.
rules.fail_condition: Welding and NDE codes overlap on a single reference line so weld length/pitch and NDE length/percentage cannot be distinguished.
rules.remediation: Place the welding symbol on the first reference line nearest the arrow and the NDE symbol on a second reference line to prevent syntactic collision.

rules.title: NDE Symbols Must Match Drawing Units; Dual Dimensioning Prohibited
rules.audit_check: The same system of units (U.S. Customary or SI) used on the drawing SHALL be used on all NDE symbols; dual dimensioning SHALL NOT be used on NDE symbols.
rules.pass_condition: All NDE length and area dimensions use a single unit system matching the drawing title block.
rules.fail_condition: NDE symbol shows dual units (e.g., 'RT 6 [150]') or mixes metric and inch dimensions.
rules.remediation: Remove dual units from NDE symbols and express all NDE dimensions solely in the drawing's primary unit system (provide a separate conversion table if needed).

rules.title: Examine-All-Around Circle Placed at Junction of Arrow and Reference Line
rules.audit_check: Examinations to be made completely around a weld, joint, or area of revolution SHALL be specified by placing the examine-all-around circle at the junction of the arrow line and the reference line.
rules.pass_condition: Examine-all-around circle is centered precisely on the bend where the arrow line meets the reference line.
rules.fail_condition: Examine-all-around circle is detached from the junction, placed at the tail, or substituted with informal text.
rules.remediation: Place the examine-all-around circle centered directly at the junction of the arrow and reference line.

rules.title: Field Examination Flag Placed at Junction of Arrow and Reference Line
rules.audit_check: Examinations to be conducted in the field (not in the shop or at the place of initial construction) SHALL be specified by placing the filled field examination flag at the junction of the arrow line and the reference line.
rules.pass_condition: Field examination flag stands vertically at the arrow-reference junction.
rules.fail_condition: Field examination flag is misplaced along the reference line, drawn hollow, or omitted when field NDE is required by notes.
rules.remediation: Place the filled field examination flag at the junction of the arrow line and reference line.

rules.title: Radiation Direction Symbol Drawn at Required Angle with Degrees Indicated
rules.audit_check: When the direction of penetrating radiation (for RT or NRT) is critical, the radiation direction symbol SHOULD be drawn on the view at the required incidence angle with the angle value indicated in degrees.
rules.pass_condition: Radiation direction symbol is oriented at the intended beam angle on the drawing view and accompanied by an explicit degree value.
rules.fail_condition: Radiation direction symbol lacks a degree angle when beam angle is non-obvious, or points in a physically obstructed direction.
rules.remediation: Draw the radiation direction symbol at the required incidence angle on the drawing view and label the angle in degrees.

rules.title: Specifications, Codes, Acceptance Criteria, and Procedures Referenced in NDE Tail
rules.audit_check: Applicable examination specifications, codes, acceptance criteria, or written procedures SHOULD be referenced in the tail of the NDE symbol (unless governed uniformly by a general drawing note).
rules.pass_condition: NDE symbol tail (or general drawing note) identifies the exact code/specification and acceptance class governing the examination.
rules.fail_condition: NDE methods such as RT, UT, PT, or MT are called out with no acceptance criteria or referenced standard anywhere on the drawing.
rules.remediation: Specify the governing NDE code, specification, and acceptance criteria in the NDE symbol tail or in the general notes.

rules.title: Partial Examined Length Placed to the Right of NDE Letter Designation
rules.audit_check: To specify examination of welds or parts where only a specific length of a section is to be examined, the length dimension SHALL be shown to the right of the NDE method letter designation.
rules.pass_condition: Examined length appears immediately to the right of the NDE letter designation (e.g., RT 6 or UT 150).
rules.fail_condition: Examined length is placed to the left of the NDE letter designation or buried in a non-standard note.
rules.remediation: Place the partial examined length immediately to the right of the NDE method letter designation.

rules.title: Exact Location and Length of Examined Section Require Dimension Lines
rules.audit_check: To show the exact location as well as the length of a section to be examined, dimension lines SHALL be used directly on the drawing.
rules.pass_condition: Localized NDE zones along a longer weld are explicitly located with dimension lines on the drawing.
rules.fail_condition: A partial examined length is specified at a critical joint region (e.g., weld intersection or highly stressed end) without drawing dimension lines showing where that length lies.
rules.remediation: Add dimension lines on the drawing to define both the exact location and length of the examined section.

rules.title: Omission of Length or Percentage Defaults to 100% Full-Length Examination
rules.audit_check: When the full length of a weld or part is to be examined, no length or percentage designation need be shown on the NDE symbol (omission defaults to 100% full-length examination).
rules.pass_condition: Omission of length or '%' aligns with 100% full-length inspection intent and does not conflict with partial-sampling notes.
rules.fail_condition: Length and '%' are omitted on the NDE symbol while a separate title-block note or specification calls for spot/10% sampling, creating a direct contradiction.
rules.remediation: Confirm 100% full-length examination is intended; if partial sampling is intended, place the percentage (e.g., 10%) to the right of the NDE code per Clause 16.10.4.

rules.title: Partial Examination (<100%) Requires Percentage Right of Code and Procedure in Tail
rules.audit_check: When less than 100% of the length of a weld or part is to be examined, with locations selected per a governing procedure, the percentage (followed by '%') SHALL be placed to the right of the NDE letter designation, and the governing selection procedure SHALL be referenced in the tail (or general notes).
rules.pass_condition: Partial percentage NDE places the percentage immediately right of the code (e.g., RT 25%, UT 10%) and references the sampling procedure in the tail or general notes.
rules.fail_condition: Percentage is placed to the left of the NDE code, omits the '%' sign (causing confusion with linear length), or omits any reference to the selection procedure.
rules.remediation: Place the exact percentage with '%' immediately to the right of the NDE method code and reference the governing selection procedure in the tail.

rules.title: Number of Random Examinations Placed in Parentheses Away from Reference Line
rules.audit_check: To specify a definite number of examinations to be conducted on a joint or part at random locations, the number SHALL be shown in parentheses above or below the NDE letter designation away from the reference line.
rules.pass_condition: Number of random examinations (e.g., (4)) is enclosed in parentheses directly below an arrow-side code, above an other-side code, or above/below a centered code.
rules.fail_condition: Examination count omits parentheses, is placed next to length/percentage, or is placed between the letter code and the reference line.
rules.remediation: Place the number of random examinations in parentheses (N) outside the NDE letter designation away from the reference line.

rules.title: Plane Area Examination Enclosed by Straight Broken Lines with Circles at Direction Changes
rules.audit_check: Plane areas to be nondestructively examined SHALL be enclosed by straight broken (dashed) lines with a small circle at each change of direction, and the area SHALL be located by coordinate dimensions when necessary.
rules.pass_condition: Examined plane areas are bounded by dashed straight lines with circles at every vertex/corner and located by coordinate dimensions.
rules.fail_condition: Plane area examination is sketched with freehand clouds, solid lines indistinguishable from part geometry, or lacks corner circles and locating coordinates.
rules.remediation: Enclose the examined plane area with straight broken lines featuring a circle at each direction change and add coordinate dimensions.

rules.title: Areas of Revolution Use Examine-All-Around Symbol Plus Appropriate Dimensions
rules.audit_check: Areas of revolution (e.g., cylindrical shells, nozzles, shafts) to be examined SHALL be indicated by the examine-all-around symbol together with appropriate axial dimensions (omission of axial dimensions specifies examination of the entire length of the surface of revolution).
rules.pass_condition: Cylindrical or conical area NDE uses the examine-all-around circle at the arrow-reference junction plus axial span dimensions when partial-length.
rules.fail_condition: Partial-length circumferential NDE on a cylinder omits axial span dimensions, or omits the examine-all-around circle when 360° coverage is intended.
rules.remediation: Add the examine-all-around symbol at the arrow-reference junction and dimension the axial span whenever less than the entire length is examined.

rules.title: Acoustic Emission (AET) Applies to Entire or Large Component Without Sensor Locations
rules.audit_check: Acoustic emission examination (AET) is generally applied to all or a large portion of a component (such as a pressure vessel or pipe); the AET symbol specifies application to the component without indicating specific sensor locations.
rules.pass_condition: AET symbol points to the vessel/component with governing test specification referenced in the tail and no unnecessary sensor-location clutter on the symbol.
rules.fail_condition: AET symbol is used without a referenced testing specification/procedure in the tail or general notes, or attempts to map localized weld lengths incompatibly.
rules.remediation: Apply the AET symbol to the target component and reference the governing acoustic emission procedure/specification in the tail.

rules.section: Annex A (Normative Tables A.1–A.6) & Annex D (Commentary Drafting Traps)
rules.title: Joint Type Letter Designators Must Conform to Table A.1
rules.audit_check: When AWS joint type letter designators are used in welding symbol tails, joint tables, or weld schedules, they SHALL conform strictly to Table A.1: B (Butt joint), C (Corner joint), T (T-joint), L (Lap joint), and E (Edge joint).
rules.pass_condition: All joint type letter codes match Table A.1 (B, C, T, L, E).
rules.fail_condition: Non-standard joint abbreviations (e.g., 'BJ', 'TEE', 'CRN', 'LP') are used where AWS Table A.1 designators are invoked.
rules.remediation: Use official AWS A2.4 Table A.1 joint designators: B, C, T, L, or E.

rules.section: Annex A (Normative Tables A.1–A.6) & Annex D (Commentary Drafting Traps)
rules.title: Welding, Brazing, Soldering, Cutting, and Allied Process Codes Must Conform to Tables A.2–A.4
rules.audit_check: Process letter designations placed in the tail of welding or brazing symbols SHALL conform to the official AWS A2.4 Tables A.2, A.3, and A.4 (126 official process and allied-process codes such as SMAW, GMAW, GTAW, FCAW, SAW, PAW, RSW, RSEW, PW, SW, EBW, LBW, FSW, TB, FB, CAC-A, PAC, OFC) rather than informal shop slang ('MIG', 'TIG', 'STICK', 'MAG', 'HELIARC', 'SUB-ARC').
rules.pass_condition: Every process abbreviation in a welding or brazing symbol tail is a valid official code from AWS A2.4 Tables A.2–A.4.
rules.fail_condition: Symbol tail contains informal slang ('MIG', 'TIG', 'STICK', 'MAG', 'HELIARC', 'ARC') or invented process codes not listed in Tables A.2–A.4.
rules.remediation: Replace informal process slang with the official AWS A2.4 Table A.2–A.4 letter designation (e.g., GMAW for MIG, GTAW for TIG, SMAW for Stick, SAW for Sub-Arc).

rules.section: Annex A (Normative Tables A.1–A.6) & Annex D (Commentary Drafting Traps)
rules.title: Optional Process Mechanization Suffixes Must Conform to Table A.5
rules.audit_check: When optional method-of-application suffixes are appended to a welding or allied process designation in the tail (e.g., GMAW-AU, GTAW-RO, SMAW-MA), they SHOULD conform to AWS A2.4 Table A.5: AD (Adaptive control), AU (Automatic), MA (Manual), ME (Mechanized), RO (Robotic), SA (Semiautomatic).
rules.pass_condition: Process suffixes in symbol tails use only valid Table A.5 two-letter codes (AD, AU, MA, ME, RO, SA).
rules.fail_condition: Informal suffixes (e.g., 'AUTO', 'MAN', 'ROBOT', 'SEMI') are appended to AWS process codes in the symbol tail.
rules.remediation: Use official AWS A2.4 Table A.5 optional suffixes: -AD, -AU, -MA, -ME, -RO, or -SA.

rules.section: Annex A (Normative Tables A.1–A.6) & Annex D (Commentary Drafting Traps)
rules.title: NDE Method Letter Designations Validation Against Table A.6
rules.audit_check: All nondestructive examination method letter codes on the drawing SHALL be validated against AWS A2.4 Table A.6 (AET, ET, LT, MP [MT in Clause 16 figures], NRT, PT, PRT, RT, UT, VT); legacy or non-AWS codes (e.g., MPI, LPI, DPI, FPI, X-RAY, EC, AE) SHALL be rejected.
rules.pass_condition: Every NDE symbol and inspection table uses valid AWS A2.4 Table A.6 letter designations.
rules.fail_condition: Drawing uses non-AWS or shop-slang NDE codes such as MPI, LPI, DPI, FPI, X-RAY, MAG, or DYEPEN.
rules.remediation: Replace all non-standard NDE abbreviations with official AWS A2.4 Table A.6 letter designations.

rules.section: Annex A (Normative Tables A.1–A.6) & Annex D (Commentary Drafting Traps)
rules.title: Changes Between Shop and Field Welding Require Formal Drawing Revision of Field Flags
rules.audit_check: Per Commentary D5.8, field weld flags communicate critical shop-vs.-field planning and shipping boundaries; whenever fabrication/erection changes move welds between shop and field, the drawing SHOULD be formally revised to add or delete field weld flags rather than relying on contradictory erection notes.
rules.pass_condition: Field weld flags on welding symbols agree completely with erection/shipping notes and assembly breakdown.
rules.fail_condition: General erection notes state 'ALL SPLICE WELDS IN FIELD' while splice welding symbols lack field weld flags (or shop-welded subassemblies carry stray field flags).
rules.remediation: Reconcile all field weld flags with shop/field assembly notes and revise affected welding symbols directly.

rules.section: Annex A (Normative Tables A.1–A.6) & Annex D (Commentary Drafting Traps)
rules.title: Prohibition of Weld-All-Around on Square/Rectangular Tubing Joints Mixing Fillet and Flare-Bevel Sides
rules.audit_check: Per Clause 5.9.2 and Commentary D5.9.2 (Figure D.1), the weld-all-around symbol SHALL NOT be used on square or rectangular tubing (HSS) T- or branch-to-header joints where the flat sides form fillet/square-groove joints and the rounded corner sides form flare-bevel-groove joints; instead, two separate welding symbols with two arrows each (one for the fillet/square-groove faces and one for the flare-bevel-groove faces) SHALL be used.
rules.pass_condition: Equal-width or flush-sided HSS/rectangular tubing joints use separate welding symbols (with dual arrows) distinguishing fillet/square-groove sides from flare-bevel-groove corner sides.
rules.fail_condition: A single fillet (or groove) welding symbol with a weld-all-around circle is applied to an equal-width rectangular/square tube joint whose corner radii create flare-bevel-groove geometry on two sides.
rules.remediation: Remove the weld-all-around symbol and specify two welding symbols with two arrows each—one for the fillet/square-groove sides and one for the flare-bevel-groove sides per Figure D.1.

rules.section: Annex A (Normative Tables A.1–A.6) & Annex D (Commentary Drafting Traps)
rules.title: Weld-All-Around Prohibited Where Weld Type/Size Changes or as Substitute for Double-Fillet/Double-Groove
rules.audit_check: Per Commentary D5.10.1, a weld-all-around symbol applies ONLY to a continuous closed-loop weld that does not change in weld type, size, or joint geometry; it SHALL NOT be used in place of a double-fillet or symmetrical double-groove symbol on opposite sides of a plate or stiffener edge.
rules.pass_condition: Weld-all-around is used strictly for continuous uniform-type/uniform-size closed-perimeter welds; opposite-side welds on open-ended joints use arrow-side and other-side weld symbols.
rules.fail_condition: Weld-all-around circle is applied to an open-ended T-joint/butt joint as shorthand for 'both sides', or applied where base-metal geometry changes weld type/size around the perimeter.
rules.remediation: Replace improper weld-all-around symbols with double-fillet or double-groove symbols (both sides of reference line), or split into distinct welding symbols wherever geometry/size changes.

rules.section: Annex A (Normative Tables A.1–A.6) & Annex D (Commentary Drafting Traps)
rules.title: 'TYPICAL' / 'TYP' Callouts Require Complete Identification of All Identical Joints
rules.audit_check: Per Commentary D5.11.3, 'TYPICAL' (or 'TYP') SHOULD be used in a welding symbol tail ONLY when all referenced joints are identical in every detail (weld type, size, geometry, and process) AND all applicable joints are completely and unambiguously identified (e.g., 'TYP AT 4 STIFFENERS' or 'TYP 6 PLACES'). Bare, unqualified 'TYP' callouts MUST be flagged as ambiguous.
rules.pass_condition: Every 'TYP' / 'TYPICAL' welding symbol explicitly identifies the exact count and locations of all identical joints it governs.
rules.fail_condition: A welding symbol tail contains bare 'TYP' or 'TYPICAL' without specifying how many joints or which features are covered, or applies to joints with differing thicknesses/geometries.
rules.remediation: Qualify every 'TYP' callout with exact count and feature identification (e.g., 'TYP AT 4 STIFFENERS') or apply explicit arrows/symbols to each joint.

rules.section: Annex A (Normative Tables A.1–A.6) & Annex D (Commentary Drafting Traps)
rules.title: Post-Backgouging U-Groove Geometry Not to Be Specified in Pre-Weld Welding Symbol
rules.audit_check: Per Commentary D5.18 (Figure D.2), when backgouging is specified in the tail of a multiple-reference-line groove weld symbol, the resulting backgouged U-groove contour is an in-process shop profile and SHOULD NOT be drawn as a separate pre-weld U-groove symbol on the opposite side of the reference line.
rules.pass_condition: Backgouged single-groove CJP joint uses the initial groove symbol on the first reference line and a back weld symbol with 'BACKGOUGE' in the tail on the second reference line.
rules.fail_condition: Welding symbol erroneously depicts a U-groove symbol on the opposite side to represent the gouged cavity created by air-carbon-arc backgouging.
rules.remediation: Replace the opposite-side U-groove glyph with a standard back weld symbol on a second reference line and specify 'BACKGOUGE' in the tail per Figure D.2.

rules.section: Annex A (Normative Tables A.1–A.6) & Annex D (Commentary Drafting Traps)
rules.title: Pre-Bid 'CJP' Symbols Omitting Joint Geometry Require Shop Construction Drawing Submittal
rules.audit_check: Per Commentary D6.2.2, when 'CJP' is placed in the tail without specifying groove type or preparation dimensions on a design/bid drawing, the drawing or contract documents SHOULD require the fabricator/bidder to submit shop construction drawings containing fully detailed welding symbols for approval; final shop/manufacturing release drawings SHOULD NOT remain with unspecified groove geometry.
rules.pass_condition: Manufacturing/shop drawings contain complete groove preparation geometry, or pre-bid design drawings using bare 'CJP' explicitly require shop drawing submittal and engineering approval.
rules.fail_condition: A released manufacturing/shop drawing uses bare 'CJP' in the tail with no groove symbol, no WPS reference, and no shop-drawing approval requirement.
rules.remediation: Specify full groove geometry (or prequalified WPS joint designation) on manufacturing drawings, or add a submittal/approval note on pre-bid design drawings.

rules.section: Annex A (Normative Tables A.1–A.6) & Annex D (Commentary Drafting Traps)
rules.title: Flare-Groove Welds Generally Cannot Achieve CJP; Obtainable Weld Size Is a Fraction of Bend Radius
rules.audit_check: Per Commentary D6.2.10 (Figure D.3), complete joint penetration (CJP) is generally NOT physically attainable in flare-V-groove or flare-bevel-groove welds because fusion occurs along curved surfaces and obtainable effective weld size (E) is only a fraction of the outside bend radius (R); calling out 'CJP' or a weld size E exceeding the physical fraction of R on a flare-groove symbol SHOULD be flagged as a manufacturability error.
rules.pass_condition: Flare-groove weld symbols specify realistic partial-joint-penetration effective weld sizes (E) compatible with the member's outside bend radius R (and do not demand CJP without special backing/qualification).
rules.fail_condition: A flare-V-groove or flare-bevel-groove welding symbol calls out 'CJP' in the tail or specifies an effective weld size E equal to or exceeding full tube wall/radius without qualification.
rules.remediation: Replace 'CJP' on flare-groove welds with a realistic effective weld size (E) consistent with the curved bend radius (per applicable structural code such as AWS D1.1/D1.3) or redesign the joint.

rules.section: Annex A (Normative Tables A.1–A.6) & Annex D (Commentary Drafting Traps)
rules.title: Bare 'SEAL WELD' Note Without Weld Type and Sizing Risks Service Cracking
rules.audit_check: Per Commentary D6.12, placing a bare 'SEAL WELD' note in the tail without specifying weld type (e.g., fillet or groove) and minimum weld size improperly delegates weld sizing to shop discretion and risks undersized welds that crack under handling, thermal cycling, vibration, or service loads; seal welds SHOULD specify an explicit weld symbol and minimum size.
rules.pass_condition: Every seal weld callout pairs the 'SEAL WELD' functional note in the tail with an explicit weld type symbol (e.g., fillet or groove) and a minimum weld size adequate for base metal thickness and service loads.
rules.fail_condition: Welding symbol specifies only 'SEAL WELD' in the tail with no weld symbol or no weld size.
rules.remediation: Add an explicit weld symbol (such as a fillet or groove symbol) and minimum weld size appropriate for the base metal thickness alongside the 'SEAL WELD' tail notation.
